  • June 2025 – 19.8 MW wind‑solar hybrid power pact with Prozeal (renewable‑energy cost hedge).
  • July 2026 – Launch of Advanced Materials unit & plan for ₹600 cr Dahej expansion into epoxy resins (capacity boost).
  • 31 Aug 2026 – Announcement to double CPVC & ECH capacity in FY27 (major scale‑up).
  • 02 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 earnings beat (profit and revenue growth).

What moves this stock

  • Growth‑target announcements (e.g., Feb 2025 revenue‑doubling plan) trigger strong upside.
  • Quarterly earnings beats (Nov 2026 Q2) produce short‑term rallies.
  • Large‑scale capex or capacity‑expansion news (Dahej epoxy plant, CPVC/ECH doubling) have mixed impact; the market often reacts cautiously, and price moves are not consistently positive.

544339.one: *De‑rated from Rs 514 to Rs 196 as post‑IPO hype faded and earnings volatility outweighed occasional upside from AI and earnings beats.*
544339.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 20 Jan 2025 – IPO debut: Shares listed at a 27 % premium (₹542) and jumped ~27 % in the first trade, lifting the price to the 2025‑Q1 high of ₹514.1.
  • 21 May 2026 – Q4 FY26 earnings: PAT surged 135 % YoY and revenue rose 16 % (announced 21 May). The stock rallied to ₹249.3 by 18 May 2026 (+32 % in four weeks).
  • 07 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 results: Record quarterly revenue (₹79.5 Cr) and 17.6 % profit growth were highlighted in the earnings call, supporting the current level around ₹196.

De‑rating factors

  • 12 Feb 2025 – Shares dip below IPO price: The first post‑IPO sell‑off saw the price fall to ₹339.3 by 24 Feb (‑32 % from the 27 Jan peak).
  • Late 2025 – early 2026: A series of unexplained declines (e.g., July‑Aug 2025, Dec 2025‑Jan 2026, Feb‑Mar 2026) have no clear headline trigger in the supplied list.
  • 21 Sep 2026 – 19 Oct 2026: The stock slipped 14 % to ₹170.2 after a flurry of marketing campaigns (Madhuri Dixit) and an analyst‑cover note, but no earnings catalyst accompanied the move.

Pivots & turning points

  • IPO (Jan 2025): First‑time public listing created a valuation benchmark.
  • Acquisition of 58 % of AI Dent (4 Aug 2025): Signaled a strategic push into AI‑driven dentistry.
  • Launch of i‑Scope360 AI‑connected platform (13 May 2026): First remote‑patient monitoring tool in the segment.
  • ESOP approvals & re‑allocation of IPO proceeds (Apr‑Sep 2026): Shifted capital toward owned manufacturing and a larger India facility.
  • Hybrid US lab strategy (Nov 2026): Target to expand capacity 3‑3.5× by FY28.

What moves this stock

  • IPO pricing & listing premium: Market reacts strongly to subscription levels and debut price.
  • Quarterly earnings beats & margin expansion: Surprising PAT or revenue growth triggers sharp short‑term rallies.
  • Strategic announcements (AI acquisitions, new platforms, capacity upgrades): Investors reward clear growth pathways, though the impact can be muted if not paired with earnings upside.

544750.html:
One‑line story: Round‑trip: debuted at a 6 % premium (~Rs 198) in April, slumped 29 % to Rs 120 in October, and clawed back to Rs 126 in early November as order wins and earnings beat were offset by a market‑wide sell‑off and a CFO resignation.

Re‑rating factors

  • 17 Apr 2026 – IPO listing: Shares opened at a 6 % premium and rose ~11 % to a 2‑yr high of Rs 198.77 on 20 Apr, driven by strong IPO demand and positive debut coverage.
  • 19 May 2026 – Q4 results: Revenue +63 % YoY, PAT +37 % (₹170 cr revenue). Despite the good numbers, the stock was already off the IPO peak, so the move was muted.
  • 7 Oct 2026 – Multiple LOIs (₹69‑78 cr) & 15 Oct 2026 – Awards (₹101‑102 cr): Large order wins lifted sentiment; the share price held above Rs 140 despite earlier weakness.

De‑rating factors

  • 27 Apr 2026 → 25 May 2026 (‑12 %): After the IPO hype faded, the stock fell from Rs 194.27 to Rs 170.69. No specific negative headline aligns; the decline appears to be profit‑taking/market‑adjustment.
  • 21 Sep 2026 → 19 Oct 2026 (‑29 %): Even with contract wins (NTPC solar, GETCO LOIs, Gujarat awards), the price dropped from Rs 168.84 to Rs 119.87. The cause isn’t evident from the headlines; broader market sell‑off (see 22 Oct low) likely drove the slide.
  • 22 Oct 2026 – “Share Price Fall” article: Stock hit a 52‑week low of Rs 142.15, confirming the downtrend.

Pivots & turning points

  • IPO launch (9‑17 Apr 2026): Pricing band ₹166‑₹175, anchor raise of >₹45 cr, and listing premium set the initial valuation.
  • July 2026 – ₹82 cr PGVCL order: First post‑IPO mega contract, gave a modest 2.3 % bump.
  • Nov 2 2026 – CFO Chetan Modi resignation & negative cash‑flow: Raised governance concerns.
  • Nov 7 2026 – Order book up to ₹839 cr & Q2 FY27 revenue +56 %: Restored some confidence, supporting the rebound to Rs 126.

What moves this stock

  • IPO‑related news: Pricing, subscription levels, and listing premium trigger sharp short‑term spikes.
  • Large transmission contracts / order wins: Positive but often insufficient to offset broader market sentiment.
  • Corporate governance events (e.g., CFO exit) and cash‑flow warnings: Prompt sell‑offs even when earnings beat expectations.

538882.one: *Round‑trip: Rs 96.75 → Rs 57.98 as early‑wage‑access and insurance‑tech partnerships, plus strong FY27 earnings, lifted the stock, while periods without clear operational news saw it tumble.*
538882.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 5 Mar 2026 – Serve2Grow early‑wage‑access tie‑up – Stock jumped from ~₹49.4 to ~₹69.2 in the next 4 weeks (+40%).
  • 19 Aug 2026 – Claycove23 Insurance‑Tech partnership (follow‑on ties with Ace Financials 11 Sep and AIC Infrastructures 27 Sep) – Share price rose from ~₹50.1 to ~₹64.7 (+29%) over the month.
  • 4 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 results (net profit +47%) – After the earnings release the price climbed from the August low of ~₹52.5 to ~₹58.0 by early Nov (+10%).

De‑rating factors

  • 3 Feb 2025 → 3 Mar 2025 – No headline – Price fell from ₹134.8 to ₹100.4 (‑26%).
  • 7 Jul 2025 → 4 Aug 2025 – No headline – Price slid from ₹94.3 to ₹72.0 (‑24%).
  • Feb 2026 → May 2026 – No headline – Share slipped from ₹65.4 to ₹63.5 (‑3%).

Pivots & turning points

  • Early‑wage‑access strategy – Partnerships with Serve2Grow, ATS Services, Unity Small Finance Bank and Automotive India (2026 Mar‑Nov).
  • Insurance‑tech collaboration – Claycove23 tie‑up (Aug 2026).
  • Capital raise – Rs 10 cr term loan from ICICI Bank (13 Jun 2026).
  • Earnings inflection – Strong Q1 FY27 profit (+52.7%) (25 Jul 2026) and Q2 FY27 profit (+47%) (4 Nov 2026).

What moves this stock

  • Early‑wage‑access partnerships – The market rewards announcements that expand employee‑product reach, delivering double‑digit price jumps.
  • Insurance‑tech and other fintech collaborations – New distribution channels for loan and insurance products trigger sharp upside.
  • Quarterly earnings beats – Surprising profit growth (Q1 & Q2 FY27) lifts the stock, while periods lacking clear operational news leave it vulnerable to declines.

522163.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 88.5 to Rs 370.6 as a wave of mega‑Adani orders, new production lines and a Rs 1,614 cr QIP turned a distressed stock into a multibagger.*
522163.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑06‑02 – Strategic partnership with US‑based TS Conductor → stock surged ~64% (Rs 100.6 → Rs 164.9 by 07 Jul 2025).
  • 2025‑05‑28 – Report of Adani talks to buy a stake (around the same time) → price jumped ~21% (Rs 93.4 → Rs 113.4 by 26 May 2025).
  • 2026‑04‑06 – 04‑15 – Multiple large Adani cable orders (₹43‑100 cr) → price rose ~32% (Rs 122.9 → Rs 161.7 by 20 Apr 2026).
  • 2026‑05‑15 – ₹55 cr investment in a 7th production line (boosting output 150 km/month) → price climbed ~23% (Rs 157.8 → Rs 194.3 by 25 May 2026).
  • 2026‑07‑05 – ₹435 cr order for data‑centre projects (upper‑circuit 10%) → price surged ~66% (Rs 222.4 → Rs 368.5 by 10 Aug 2026).
  • 2026‑07‑29 – Rs 1,614 cr QIP at 5 % discount (debt repayment) → reinforced the up‑trend into Oct‑Nov 2026.

De‑rating factors

  • 2024‑12‑30 – 2025‑01‑27 – No headline‑linked event; price fell ~32% (Rs 150.8 → Rs 102.4).
  • 2025‑02‑24 – Low of Rs 85.8 (no matching news) – the dip to the 2025‑02 quarterly low remains unexplained.
  • 2026‑02‑13 – Analyst note “business trailing industry” → price slipped to Rs 124.4 by Feb 2026 (cause not clear from headlines).

Pivots & turning points

  • June 2025: First major partnership (TS Conductor) and stake‑sale by Monarch/GSEC – signalled a strategic shift toward higher‑value conductors.
  • July 2025: Rs 1,349 cr Adani order – cemented the Adani‑centric order book.
  • Sept‑Oct 2025: Series of Adani Energy & Green Energy orders (₹236‑₹748 cr) expanded revenue base.
  • Nov 2025: Approval of Rs 1,000 cr QIP – provided growth capital.
  • Sept 2026: Early exit from NCLT (₹2,401 cr plan) cleared legal cloud.
  • Aug 2026: Commissioning of 1,500 MT/month copper line – diversification into copper‑conductor cables.

What moves this stock

  • Large‑scale orders from the Adani Group (multi‑crore cable and conductor contracts).
  • Capacity‑expansion announcements (new production lines, copper‑cable line, polymer complex).
  • Equity‑raising events (QIP launches) that signal strong balance‑sheet support and enable order fulfilment.

538268.one: *De‑rated from Rs ≈ 900 to Rs ≈ 477 as the market rewarded expansion milestones but punished profit‑margin squeezes and operational hiccups.*
538268.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Aug 4‑10 2026 – Record Q1 FY27: “Wonderla posts record Q1 with 41 % rise in revenue” and “Chennai park drives expansion” → price jumped from ~ 477 Rs to ~ 537 Rs (+12 %).
  • Apr 14 2026 – Terrea resort launch: “Wonderla launches Terrea, an Earth‑inspired urban resort” → modest uptick in sentiment (price held above Rs 550).

De‑rating factors

  • Dec 2‑30 2024 – 15 % fall (899 → 762 Rs): No headline directly tied to the move; cause isn’t clear from the listed news.
  • Jan 20‑Feb 17 2025 – 17 % fall (765 → 634 Rs): No contemporaneous headline; cause isn’t clear from the listed news.
  • Apr 13‑May 11 2026 – 14 % fall (550 → 473 Rs): Around the same time “Why Is Wonderla Holidays Share Price Falling” (May 5) and Q4 results showing revenue up 13 % but net profit down 25 % (May 8) → profit‑margin worries drove the slide.

Pivots & turning points

  • Dec 2 2025 – Chennai park opening: First park in Tamil Nadu, “India’s tallest spin ride” (multiple Dec 2025 headlines).
  • Apr 14 2026 – Terrea resort debut: First premium‑hospitality brand extension.
  • Aug 4‑10 2026 – Record Q1 FY27: 41 % revenue jump, EBITDA up 90 % (turning profit).
  • Nov 2‑7 2026 – Q2 FY27 profit: Revenue +45 %, EBITDA +90 % (first full‑quarter profit).

What moves this stock

  • New park or resort launches (Chennai, Terrea, Garuda Glide) – market reacts positively when the asset is operational and draws footfall.
  • Quarterly earnings surprises – strong top‑line growth lifts the stock, but any profit‑margin deterioration or cost‑inflation news drags it down.
  • Operational or regulatory setbacks (cyclone‑related opening chaos, GST notice, NGT encroachment case) – these generate short‑term sell‑offs.

543328.one: *De‑rated from Rs 939.65 to Rs 475 as margin pressure, soaring receivables and mixed contract news eroded confidence.*
543328.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑07‑08 – Fresh Letter of Award from Rajasthan – price jumped from ≈ ₹698 to ₹853 (+22 %) in the following 4 weeks.
  • 2026‑09‑16/17 – 15‑year PET‑CT concession in Punjab – shares surged ~10‑11 % on 17 Sept 2026; the deal opened a new high‑margin service line.

De‑rating factors

  • 2024‑12‑26 – “What Krsnaa Diagnostics got right” (published after the 13 % fall from ₹996 to ₹868, 25 Nov – 23 Dec 2024). No clear catalyst; the drop appears unrelated to headlines.
  • 2025‑01‑27 – 2025‑02‑24 – 18 % fall to ₹710 – no contemporaneous news; cause isn’t evident from the headlines.
  • 2025‑04‑14 – MD Yash Mutha appointed – price fell 19 % to ₹647 by 12 May 2025, suggesting market uncertainty around the leadership change.
  • 2025‑10‑06 – 2025‑11‑03 – 12 % decline to ₹724 – no specific news in this window; the move is unexplained by the list.
  • 2026‑02‑23 – 2026‑03‑23 – 14 % drop to ₹547 – coincides with BoD re‑appointing Rajendra Mutha as executive chairman (23 Feb & 16 Mar 2026), possibly signalling governance concerns.
  • Oct 2026 – AI partnership with AZmed – shares opened in red and continued sliding, contributing to the slide toward the 2026‑11 low of ₹475.

Pivots & turning points

  • Leadership: MD change (Apr 2024) and executive‑chairman re‑appointment (Feb‑Mar 2026).
  • Contract wins: Rajasthan award (Jul 2025) and Punjab PET‑CT concession (Sep 2026).
  • Strategic shift: AI collaboration with AZmed (Oct 2026).
  • Financial pressure: Q2 FY27 record revenue but margin contraction, 61 % receivable rise (Nov 2026).
  • Operational disruption: Shimla strike (Nov 2026) and equipment‑sale plan (Sep 2026).

What moves this stock

  • Large government contracts (Rajasthan, Punjab PET‑CT) trigger sharp upside.
  • Margin or earnings pressure (high receivables, margin contraction) drives downside.
  • Strategic partnerships or governance news (AI tie‑up, chair‑person changes) create volatility, often negative when the market perceives execution risk.

500245.one: *De‑rated from Rs 452 to Rs 385 as margin‑pressured guidance and plant shutdowns erased the upside from a $13.5 m export win and capacity‑expansion news.*
500245.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 18 Jun 2026 – $13.5 m export order: “Kirloskar Ferrous Industries jumps 12% after bagging $13.5 million export order” → share price surged from ~₹435 to the 4‑week high of ₹489.65 (‑ 12 % move).
  • 08 May 2026 – Q4 FY26 profit +36 %: “Kirloskar Ferrous Q4FY26 Net Profit Jumps 36% to ₹130 Cr” → price climbed from the low‑₹430s to ₹452.2 by early April 2026.
  • 01 Jun 2026 – USD 52 m capacity spend: “Kirloskar Ferrous Industries To Invest USD 52 Million To Increase Seamless Tube Production Capacity” → reinforced the June rally, keeping the stock above the ₹460 level.

De‑rating factors

  • 30 Sep 2026 – Hiriyur plant suspension (15 days): “Kirloskar Ferrous suspends Hiriyr plant operations for 15 days” → market sentiment soured; price slid from the ₹458‑range in early October toward the ₹385.4 low on 2 Nov.
  • 07 Nov 2026 – Cautious Q2 FY27 call: “Management cited continued margin pressures … despite sequential volume and revenue growth” → the warning coincided with the sharp ‑16 % 4‑week decline (458.7 → 385.4).

Pivots & turning points

  • May 2026 – ESOP allotment & ₹1,000 cr NCD raise (capital‑structure boost).
  • Mar 2026 – Merger scheme approval for subsidiaries (streamlining).
  • Jun 2026 – Capacity expansion + export order (growth catalyst).
  • Sep 2026 – Joint Managing Director appointment (leadership change).
  • Oct‑Nov 2026 – Plant maintenance suspensions & cautious guidance (operational drag).

What moves this stock

  • Large export or contract wins (e.g., $13.5 m order) trigger immediate upside.
  • Capacity‑expansion announcements (USD 52 m spend) are positively priced in.
  • Operational disruptions or soft guidance (plant shutdowns, margin‑pressure cautions) pull the stock sharply lower.

543989.one: Round‑trip from Rs 161 → Rs 185 → Rs 111 → Rs 117 → Rs 89 as a strategic merger, earnings surprises and aggressive store‑roll‑outs drove the swings.
543989.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑10‑15 – Strategic merger with Kalamandir Fashions – price jumped from ~Rs 152 to ~Rs 187 (+23 %) by 2025‑10‑20.
  • 2026‑05‑08 – “Ticks all the boxes” earnings‑growth story – price rose from Rs 95.6 to Rs 117.3 (+23 %) by 2026‑05‑04, helped by Q4 FY26 results (05‑13) and the appointment of CEO Bharadwaj Rachamadugu (05‑14/16).
  • 2026‑10‑05 – Q2 FY27 turnover of ₹434 Cr & opening of 4 new stores – price climbed from Rs 73.8 to Rs 89.0 (+21 %) by 2026‑11‑06, reinforced by further store openings (10‑31) and a festive‑demand upbeat earnings call (11‑04).

De‑rating factors

  • 2025‑02‑10 → 2025‑03‑10 – 21 % drop (Rs 161 → Rs 127) – no headline directly coincides; the cause isn’t clear from the listed news.
  • 2025‑12‑29 → 2026‑01‑26 – 27 % fall (Rs 152 → Rs 111) – follows “Earnings working against share price” (2026‑01‑22) after a 28 % earnings dive.
  • 2026‑06‑12 – “Why share price falling” article – preceded a modest dip, but no specific price level is given in the 4‑week list; the move is attributed to earnings weakness.

Pivots & turning points

  • Strategic merger (15 Oct 2025) – created a clear growth narrative.
  • CEO change (mid‑May 2026) – signalled fresh leadership and operational focus.
  • Accelerated store network (Aug‑Oct 2026) – 85th‑87th stores opened, boosting same‑store sales outlook.
  • Festive‑season demand shift (Dussehra calendar change, Q2 FY27) – highlighted in the November 2026 earnings call.

What moves this stock

  • M&A announcements – the Oct 2025 merger sparked the strongest rally.
  • Quarterly earnings surprises – both beats (May 2026) and misses (Jan 2026) produced >20 % moves.
  • Store‑expansion and festive‑season updates – new openings and positive festive demand consistently lifted the share price.

544512.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 189.6 to Rs 309.5 as a premium IPO debut, bridal‑segment expansion and a Buy rating lifted the stock, while a March‑2026 slump remains unexplained.*
544512.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Sep 10‑17 2025 – IPO debut: Shares listed at a 14 % premium; price jumped from ~Rs 188 to Rs 225 (+20 % in 4 weeks).
  • Dec 24 2025 – Visionary Vendor Partner award (Indriya): Helped push the price from Rs 196 to Rs 231 (+17 % Dec 08‑Jan 05).
  • Apr 7‑9 2026 – Entry into gold bridal jewellery: Announcement of a strategic expansion lifted the price from Rs 192 to Rs 225 (+17 % Apr 06‑May 04).
  • Sep 29 2026 – Bridal‑foray & capacity ramp‑up: News of a new bridal line and 4,000 kg capacity boost drove the price from Rs 211 to Rs 314 (+49 % Sep 14‑Oct 12).
  • Oct 5 2026 – IIFA manufacturer award & Oct 30 2026 – Analyst “Buy” rating: Reinforced the rally, keeping the stock near its 2‑year high.

De‑rating factors

  • Feb 23‑Mar 23 2026 – 23 % slide to Rs 175.9: No headline directly coincides; the cause isn’t clear from the available news.

Pivots & turning points

  • Feb 10 2025 – DRHP filing → Sep 10 2025 – IPO opens → Sep 17 2025 – Listing at 14 % premium.
  • Jun 19 2025 – First Delhi branch; Jan 27 2026 – Pune sales office (geographic expansion).
  • Apr 7 2026 – Strategic entry into gold bridal jewellery (new product line).
  • Nov 5‑7 2026 – Q2 FY27 results: Revenue +55 %, profit +73 % (strong earnings backdrop).
  • Nov 5 2026 – Capacity raised to 4,000 kg (operational scaling).

What moves this stock

  • IPO‑related milestones (filing, subscription, premium listing) trigger sharp upside.
  • New segment launches (gold bridal jewellery, bridal‑foray) generate strong rallies.
  • Analyst upgrades and industry awards (Buy rating, IIFA award) add further momentum.

When none of these catalysts appear, price action can be erratic, as seen in the unexplained March‑2026 dip.

544367.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 302.7 to Rs 1,363.5 as a string of strategic international orders, new‑capacity roll‑outs and strong earnings repeatedly lifted the share price.*
544367.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • May 17 2025 – Strategic 4‑yr framework order (161 kV coil) & May 28 record order backlog – price jumped from ₹346.3 (28 Apr) to ₹481.9 (26 May) (+39%).
  • June 27 2025 – New coil factory opened in Sangli – price surged from ₹502.1 (9 Jun) to ₹776.8 (7 Jul) (+55%).
  • Sept 25 2025 – Hyosung GIS JV agreement & Sept 30 2025 ₹139.4 m HV‑air‑core reactor order – price rose from ₹784.1 (25 Aug) to ₹1,013.5 (22 Sep) (+29%).
  • Feb 27 2026 – Fresh ₹34 Cr HVDC reactor orders (plus FY26 revenue guidance on 23 Feb) – price climbed from ₹598.0 (19 Jan) to ₹882.5 (16 Feb) (+48%).
  • Mar 27‑28 2026 – International BESS order worth ₹1.52 bn – price leapt from ₹861.5 (23 Mar) to ₹1,396.4 (20 Apr) (+62%).
  • Aug 9‑10 2026 – Q1 FY27 profit up 47% and order book at ₹1,945 cr – price rose from ₹1,124.1 (3 Aug) to ₹1,495.3 (31 Aug) (+33%).

De‑rating factors

  • Feb 24 2025 – IPO debut: shares listed at a 2 % premium then fell ~10 % on day 1 – early‑stage sell‑off after listing.
  • May 14 2025 – “IPO buzz fizzles” headline – contributed to short‑term weakness in the post‑IPO period.
  • May 06 2026 – Analyst note on price pull‑back after a sharp rally – reflected a brief corrective dip despite strong fundamentals.

Pivots & turning points

  • Feb 2025 IPO and listing – created a public market for the company.
  • Mar 8 2025 – Acquisition of majority stake in Mehru Engineering – expanded product mix.
  • June 2025 – Ground‑breaking and commissioning of the Sangli coil plant – added ~30 % capacity.
  • Mar‑Apr 2026 – Securing a ₹1.52 bn battery‑storage (BESS) contract – diversified into high‑growth storage segment.
  • Aug 2026 – Q1 FY27 earnings beat (PAT +47 %) and strong order book – reinforced growth narrative.
  • Oct 2026 – Start of production at new Sangli coil factory – operationalised the capacity expansion.

What moves this stock

  • Award of large international/high‑voltage orders (e.g., Israeli coil framework, US order, BESS contract) → immediate price spikes.
  • Announcements of new manufacturing capacity or plant commissioning → bullish re‑ratings.
  • Quarterly earnings that beat expectations and show margin expansion → sustained upward momentum.

Overall, Quality Power’s share price has been driven primarily by the pipeline of sizable overseas contracts and the rollout of new production facilities, with earnings beats providing the final push. The market penalises only short‑term setbacks such as IPO‑day volatility or temporary sentiment dips.

544046.one: *Re‑rated from Rs ≈ 903 to Rs ≈ 2,250 as a cascade of large industrial, LNG and space‑sector orders, plus record‑breaking earnings, lifted the stock, while a few unexplained dips trimmed the rally.*
544046.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Mar 7 2025 – “INOX India Ltd Bags Multiple Orders” → price jumped from ~₹916 to ~₹1,050 (+15%) in the following 4 weeks.
  • May 16 2025 – FY25 results (PAT + 15.4%) → price surged from ₹979 to ₹1,220 (+25%) by early June 2025, reinforced by the ₹373 Cr order win on Jun 17.
  • Apr 16 2026 – Analyst note: shares up 20% in 3 sessions → price climbed from ~₹1,180 to ~₹1,490 (+26%) as Q4‑2026 results and the first cryogenic tanks shipped to the Bahamas (Apr 21) hit headlines.
  • May 12‑21 2026 – Q4 profit + 15%, revenue + 24% and ₹322 Cr new orders → price leapt from ~₹1,448 to ~₹1,918 (+32%) in the next month.
  • Aug 3‑9 2026 – Q1 FY27 revenue record, orbital‑welding order (Sep 22) → price rose from ~₹1,943 to ~₹2,247 (+16%) as the order backlog hit a record ₹2,268 Cr.

De‑rating factors

  • Dec 30 2024 – Jan 27 2025 – 17% drop (₹1,103 → ₹917) – no matching headline; cause isn’t clear from the provided news.
  • Feb 2025 low (₹972) – no specific event in the list explains the dip.

Pivots & turning points

  • Entry into clean‑energy hardware: launch of India’s first UHP ammonia ISO tank (Jun 13 2025) and the LNG‑fuelled cryogenic tanker (Dec 25 2025).
  • Space‑sector breakthrough: multiple space‑related orders (July 2026) and the first orbital‑welding contract (Sep 22 2026).
  • Record order backlog: highlighted in the Q2 FY27 call (Nov 7 2026) – now > ₹2,200 Cr.
  • Diversification into semiconductors & water solutions: semiconductor training centre (Oct 26 2026) and water‑solutions JV with Sweden’s Wayout (Jun 29 2026).

What moves this stock

  • Large, multi‑segment order wins (industrial gas, LNG, space, semiconductor) – each win triggers a 10‑30% rally within weeks.
  • Milestone product launches (UHP ammonia tanks, cryogenic LNG tanks, first LNG‑fuelled tanker) – boost investor confidence and drive price spikes.
  • Strong earnings beats & record backlog announcements – earnings calls and analyst notes that flag record revenue or backlog generate sharp upside moves.

544742.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 405.7 to Rs 618.6 as the IPO premium and a blockbuster Australian OTC contract lifted expectations, then de‑rated to Rs 466.35 amid profit‑taking and a quiet news flow.*
544742.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2026‑04‑02 – IPO debut at a 3 % premium (₹392) – shares listed at a premium to the price band and jumped from ~₹405 to ₹486 by 27 Apr (+20 % in 4 weeks).
  • 2026‑07‑01/02 – ₹1,300 cr Australian OTC medicines deal (Noumed subsidiary) – the announcement of a multi‑hundred‑crore supply contract coincided with the stock climbing to its 2‑year high of ₹618.6 on 29 Jun (+22 % from mid‑May).
  • 2026‑08‑12 – Q1 FY27 results (₹182 cr revenue, PAT +464 % YoY) – strong earnings reinforced the upside narrative; price held above the June peak for a short spell.
  • 2026‑11‑02 – 07 – Q2 FY27 results (Revenue +9 % QoQ, EBITDA +67 % QoQ) – earnings beat kept the stock above the ₹460 level despite earlier declines.

De‑rating factors

  • 2026‑09‑30 – Management change (new CS & COO after resignation) – share price slipped from the June high to ₹523.6 by early Sept; the move is not directly explained by headlines.
  • Late‑Oct/Nov profit‑taking – after the July‑August rally, the stock drifted to ₹466.35 by 6 Nov; no specific negative news, so the pull‑back appears driven by market‑wide profit‑taking.

Pivots & turning points

  • IPO (Mar‑Apr 2026) – capital raise of >₹122 cr and listing premium.
  • Acquisition of Noumed (Dec 2025) – entry into Australian OTC market.
  • July 2026 Australian contract win – transformed revenue outlook.
  • Capacity expansion to 155 Mn units/month (Nov 2026) – enabled CDMO‑led export model.
  • Prathyak Labs stake (Aug‑Oct 2026) – further diversification.

What moves this stock

  • IPO pricing & listing premium – the market reacts strongly to subscription levels and debut price.
  • Large overseas contract announcements – especially Australian OTC supply deals that signal multi‑year revenue streams.
  • Quarterly earnings beats & margin expansion – robust top‑line growth and EBITDA improvement translate into short‑term price lifts.

512008.one: *De‑rated from Rs 336.95 to Rs 165.12 as profit‑driven optimism faded and a series of capital‑raising, de‑merger and acquisition moves failed to sustain the rally.*
512008.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑11‑11 – Strong Q2 FY26 results (55 % net‑profit jump) – price climbed from ~Rs 270 to Rs 308 by 2025‑12‑15 (+14 %).
  • 2025‑08‑19 – NSE debut (august 20) – share surged to the 2025‑08 high of Rs 336.95 as the listing broadened the investor base.

De‑rating factors

  • 2025‑12‑22 – 2026‑01‑19 – Profit‑take after the November rally – price fell from Rs 299 to Rs 240 (‑20 %). No specific negative headline; the drop appears unexplained by the available news.
  • 2026‑02‑16 – 2026‑03‑16 – Earnings‑preview anxiety – price slid from Rs 263 to Rs 196 (‑26 %). The move coincides with the 2026‑03‑19 earnings preview that hinted at softer outlook, but no concrete adverse event is listed.

Pivots & turning points

  • 2025‑03‑05 – JV incorporation (Forty Two Ventures) – signaled diversification.
  • 2025‑10‑28 – Rs 20 cr loan converted to convertible debentures – altered capital structure.
  • 2025‑11‑05/‑14 – Share‑capital increase & promoter re‑classification – aimed at improving liquidity and governance perception.
  • 2026‑04‑03/‑07 – Rights issue approved (up to Rs 160 cr at Rs 150/share) – large equity raise that pressured the stock.
  • 2026‑07‑29 – Demerger of asset‑light office business – strategic split to unlock value.
  • 2026‑08‑13/‑18 – Acquisition of Ultrafresh (₹54 cr all‑share swap) – entry into modular solutions, followed by a secondary share issue at Rs 270/share.
  • 2026‑11‑03 – Q2 FY27 results (PAT +36 %) and equity issuance – strong earnings but price remained at the 2026‑11 low.

What moves this stock

  • Earnings surprises – large profit jumps (e.g., Nov 2025) trigger sharp short‑term rallies.
  • Capital‑structure events – rights issues, convertible debentures, and share‑capital changes tend to depress the price as dilution concerns dominate.
  • Strategic restructurings – de‑mergers or big acquisitions (Ultrafresh) create volatility; the market rewards clear value‑creation rationale but penalises execution uncertainty.

544030.html:
De‑rated from Rs 276.7 to Rs 248.73 as a mid‑2026 earnings surge was eclipsed by flood‑related cost pressure, raw‑material inflation and governance changes.

Re‑rating factors

  • 21 May 2026 – FY26 earnings beat – Revenue up 15.8 % and PAT up 18.7 % (steel‑bottle & creative lines). Share price climbed to a 2‑year high of Rs 337.55 by early May.
  • 22 Jun 2026 – Rs 20 cr retail order win – Momentum in the Creative & Houseware businesses reinforced the bullish sentiment from the May earnings, helping the stock hold above the Rs 300 mark through June.

De‑rating factors

  • 01 Jul 2026 – “Why Is Flair Writing Industries Share Price Falling?” – Market commentary flagged raw‑material inflation and looming supply‑chain strains; the stock slid from Rs 334 (11 May) to Rs 270.45 (08 Jun).
  • 28 Sep 2026 – Board changes – Management reshuffle added uncertainty; price drifted down to Rs 252.4 (08 Aug) and lingered near Rs 248‑250 thereafter.
  • 07 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 results – Profit fell 26 % YoY on flood‑related factory shutdowns and higher input costs; the share closed the period at Rs 248.73.

Pivots & turning points

  • Feb 2026 – Launch of wooden‑pencil line (8.4 cr capacity). First foray beyond traditional steel‑bottle & creative products.
  • 11 Aug 2026 – Announcement of a fourth steel‑bottle line (Q4 FY27). Signaled capacity expansion.
  • 01 Sep 2026 – ₹100 cr rights issue subscription. Strengthened balance sheet for growth plans.
  • Nov 2026 – Flood disruptions & raw‑material price spikes (highlighted in Q2 FY27 call).

What moves this stock

  • Earnings surprises – Strong top‑line and profit growth (e.g., May 2026) trigger sharp upside.
  • Product‑line expansions – New manufacturing capacity (wooden pencils, extra steel‑bottle line) is rewarded when announced.
  • Operational setbacks & governance news – Flood‑related losses, raw‑material inflation, and board changes prompt noticeable downside.

532321.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 831.55 (Apr 2025 low) to Rs 1,197.9 (Nov 2026) as FDA approvals, strategic acquisitions and first‑in‑India biosimilar launches lifted the stock, while regulatory observations and profit‑misses pulled it back.*
532321.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Late Apr – May 2026: May 2 – acquisition of France‑based Aptitude Orthopedie; May 5 – clean USFDA inspection at Ahmedabad plant (shares +3%); May 14 – $166 m acquisition of US oncology firm Assertio. 4‑week rally from ₹891.9 to ₹1,077.7 (+21%).
  • Oct 21 2026: USFDA approval for a Hormone Patch → price surged to the 2‑yr high of ₹1,245.5 on Oct 26.
  • Feb – Mar 2026: Feb 19 – launch of India’s first aflibercept biosimilar (Anyra); Feb 26 – launch of Semaglutide Injection; Mar 2 – USFDA final approvals for Ivermectin & Dapsone tablets → stock climbed to ₹940 in May and to ₹1,114 by Aug.
  • Jul 3 2026: MoU with Apollo Hospitals & Guardant Health for a multi‑cancer detection test → shares up ~3% to a 52‑wk high.
  • Aug 11 2026: Q1 FY27 results showed 22% revenue growth despite a 36% profit dip; investors rewarded the top‑line momentum, shares jumped 5‑6%.

De‑rating factors

  • Oct 13 2026: USFDA inspection at Ahmedabad plant returned 5 observations → stock slipped ~2%.
  • Nov 4 2026: Q2 FY27 profit fell 27% after a 52‑wk high → shares down >4%.
  • Jun 3 2026: USFDA warning letter to the Baddi formulation unit → negative sentiment.
  • Apr 2 2026: Rs 1.42 cr tax demand announced → modest drag.
  • Oct 8 2026: Supreme Court request to Centre (regulatory uncertainty) → top losers fell up to 3%.

Pivots & turning points

  • Strategic M&A: Aptitude Orthopedie (May 2026), Assertio (May 2026), Zara Merger Sub (Apr 2026) aimed at a 50% US revenue contribution.
  • Regulatory milestones: Multiple USFDA approvals (Baddi plant, Hormone Patch, biosimilars) and clean inspection reports.
  • Product launches: First indigenously developed aflibercept biosimilar, Semaglutide injection, and US generic launches (Adempas, Ivermectin).
  • Capital actions: ₹5,000 cr QIP (Nov 2025) and entry into China (Nov 2025).
  • Partnerships: Apollo Hospitals cancer‑test pact (Jul 2026) and Sri Lanka JV (Jun 2026).

What moves this stock

  • USFDA outcomes – clean inspections and new approvals trigger sharp rallies; observations or warning letters cause immediate pull‑backs.
  • Acquisition & partnership announcements – especially those expanding US/International footprint, lift the share price.
  • First‑in‑India biosimilar launches – generate enthusiasm and price appreciation, reflecting growth potential in high‑margin specialty segments.

540403.one: *De‑rated from Rs 126.8 to Rs 55.1 as the market punished post‑acquisition integration worries and a 2026 risk scare, then re‑rated on strong Q2 FY27 earnings and cost‑cutting wins.*
540403.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 14 May 2026 – Q4 2026 results: Revenue jumped 21% to ₹118 cr and the loss narrowed; the stock rallied from ₹39.8 → ₹53.8 (+35 %) over the next 4 weeks.
  • 3‑7 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 earnings: PAT surged 59 % to ₹8.2 cr, EBITDA margin rose 300 bps and overhead cuts delivered ₹20.5 cr savings; the share climbed to ₹55 by 6 Nov.
  • 15‑16 Oct 2026 – Upper‑circuit & rating news: ICRA’s BBB rating and a brief upper‑circuit run lifted the price 3‑4 % in a single day, showing sensitivity to credit‑rating upgrades.

De‑rating factors

  • 31 Jan 2025 – NSEIT digital‑exam acquisition announced (₹230 cr): The stock peaked at ₹126.8 on 27 Jan, then fell sharply to ₹75.2 by 24 Feb (‑41 %). The drop coincided with market concerns over integration risk and valuation stretch.
  • 7 Feb 2026 – “Riskier Than It Looks” article: A bearish analyst note (down 28 %) appeared just as the price slid from ₹73.7 to a 2‑year low of ₹39.4 by 23 Feb (‑46 %). No fundamental news offset the negative sentiment.

Pivots & turning points

  • Jan 2025 – Completion of NSEIT acquisition (4 Feb). Marked a strategic shift into digital exam assessment.
  • 19 Oct 2026 – Approval of merger of subsidiary DEXIT Global. Signals a move toward NEET CBT platform.
  • 5 Oct 2026 – Plan to raise ₹100 cr via NCDs for debt refinance. Improves balance‑sheet flexibility.
  • Nov 2026 – Cost‑optimization program lifts H1 EBITDA margin to 18.6 % and drives profit rebound.

What moves this stock

  • Acquisition & integration news – the NSEIT deal sparked a big rally‑then‑sell‑off cycle.
  • Quarterly earnings surprises – margin expansion, profit turn‑around and cost‑cut announcements generate sharp upside.
  • Credit‑rating or risk commentary – downgrades or risk‑focused articles can trigger steep downside, as seen in Feb 2026.

540710.one: *De‑rated from Rs 441.45 to Rs 180.1 as large contract wins lifted the stock temporarily but a series of unexplained sell‑offs drove it lower.*
540710.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 14 Feb 2025 – Rs 1,320 cr NBCC contract – price rose from ~₹365 (Nov 2024) to ₹376.25 by Feb 2025.
  • 4 Jun 2026 – ₹589 cr civil works order from Raymond Realty – price climbed to ₹252.5 in May 2026 (up from ₹233.25 in Feb 2026).
  • 6 Oct 2026 – ₹369 cr Chennai Metro Rail order – shares jumped ≈4.6 % on the day (price still above the low of ₹145.7 later in Oct).
  • 4 Nov 2026 – Letter of award for ₹3.06 bn from Puravankara + Q2 FY27 results (19 % revenue rise) – price recovered to ₹180.1 by early Nov 2026 after hitting a low of ₹145.7 on 26 Oct.

De‑rating factors

  • 23 Dec 2024 → 20 Jan 2025 – 20 % drop (₹441.45 → ₹354.25) – no headline aligns; cause unclear.
  • 9 Feb 2026 → 9 Mar 2026 – 27 % drop (₹258.1 → ₹189.4) – no contemporaneous news; cause unclear.
  • 22 Jun 2026 → 20 Jul 2026 – 20 % drop (₹264.15 → ₹212.75) – despite the June ₹589 cr order, price fell; cause unclear.
  • 21 Sep 2026 → 19 Oct 2026 – 22 % drop (₹191.3 → ₹149.25) – after the Oct 6 Metro order, price still slid; cause unclear.

Pivots & turning points

  • Large‑scale contract wins (NBCC, Raymond Realty, Chennai Metro, Puravankara) – each created short‑term rallies.
  • LOIs (₹537 cr TenX Realty, ₹741 cr Mahindra Lifespace) – signalled pipeline growth but did not prevent later declines.
  • Executive appointments (9 Oct 2026) – signaled management refresh; no immediate price impact.
  • Q2 FY27 earnings call (7 Nov 2026) – highlighted record revenue and execution, supporting the modest rebound in Nov 2026.

What moves this stock

  • Announcement of multi‑crore construction contracts – the market reacts positively, often with single‑digit to low‑double‑digit jumps.
  • Quarterly earnings that beat revenue expectations – even with margin pressure, revenue growth lifts sentiment.
  • Major pipeline updates (LOIs, letters of award) – investors price in future order flow, though the effect can be short‑lived if broader market sentiment is weak.

532548.one: *De‑rated from ~₹ 835 to ~₹ 639 as strong growth hopes were offset by capacity‑expansion jitters and mixed earnings signals.*
532548.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑04‑09 – HDFC Securities “Buy” call, TP ₹1,005 – price climbed from ₹ 675.3 (05‑05) to ₹ 789.2 (06‑02) (+17%) in the following weeks.
  • 2025‑05‑27 – Genefied partnership – reinforced the “growth‑above‑15%” narrative; price kept its upward trajectory into early June.
  • 2026‑04‑22 – Management expects stable margins as MDF price hikes offset cost surge – price jumped from ₹ 650.9 (03‑16) to ₹ 762.15 (04‑13) (+17%) as investors priced in margin protection.

De‑rating factors

  • 2025‑02‑03 to 2025‑03‑03 – price fell from ₹ 865.75 to ₹ 738.45 (‑15%) – no headline directly coincides; the cause isn’t clear from the listed news.
  • 2026‑02‑09 to 2026‑03‑09 – price slid from ₹ 765.6 to ₹ 659.45 (‑14%) – around the same time the company announced a new Odisha manufacturing unit (01‑31, 02‑02, 02‑04) and the resignation of Plant Head Ashok Kumar Goyal (02‑07), sparking execution‑risk concerns.
  • 2024‑11‑11 to 2024‑12‑09 – price rose 12% but no contemporaneous news – cause not evident from headlines.

Pivots & turning points

  • July 2025 – Commissioning of India’s largest particle‑board plant (Tamil Nadu/Chennai).
  • Jan‑Feb 2026 – Exploration of a new Odisha unit and later a ₹ 870 cr capex plan (May 2026).
  • Oct 2026 – Launch of a ₹ 215 cr greenfield plywood facility in Punjab (Hoshiarpur).
  • Nov 2026 – Record Q2 FY27 revenue (₹ 1,780 cr) and 46% profit jump; simultaneous ESG reporting and “Total Cover” warranty launch with Aamir Khan.

What moves this stock

  • Capacity‑expansion announcements (new plants in Odisha, Punjab, and the 2025 particle‑board launch) swing sentiment sharply.
  • Earnings beats and margin guidance (HDFC buy rating, FY26 profit jumps, stable‑margin outlook) trigger strong upside moves.
  • Analyst upgrades / strategic partnerships (HDFC “Buy”, Genefied collaboration) are rewarded, while leadership changes or execution‑risk news (e.g., plant‑head resignation) pull the stock down.

543299.one: *De‑rated from Rs 711 (Feb 2025) to Rs 1 301 (Nov 2026) as the market rewarded successive capacity‑expansion and new‑business announcements, while a brief dip in early 2026 lacked a clear headline trigger.*
543299.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 13 Mar 2025 – Roofing & new‑business launch in West Bengal – Share price jumped from ≈ Rs 711 to ≈ Rs 853 (+20 % in 4 weeks).
  • 20 Apr 2026 – Pakuria annealing furnaces & CRM capacity boost to 0.40 MTPA – Stock rose from ≈ Rs 821 to ≈ Rs 948 (+16 % in 4 weeks).
  • 05 Oct 2026 – MoU with Maharashtra for a ₹50 000 cr integrated steel complex + mining‑rights win (Oct 13) – Shares surged from ≈ Rs 1 060 to ≈ Rs 1 301 (+23 % in 4 weeks).
  • 07 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 earnings beat expectations (revenues, EBITDA & PAT up YoY) – Reinforced the upward trend, keeping the stock near its 2‑yr high.

De‑rating factors

  • 09 Feb 2026 → 09 Mar 2026 – Price fell from ≈ Rs 879 to ≈ Rs 770 (‑12 %). No headline in the list directly coincides; the cause isn’t clear from the available news.

Pivots & turning points

  • Mar 2025: Entry into roofing sheets & wagon‑manufacturing (greenfield plant at Kharagpur).
  • Oct 2025: Commissioning of advanced cold‑rolling mill in West Bengal; Phase I of Jamuria CRM started.
  • Apr 2026: Launch of a 60 000 TPA aluminium facility in Sambalpur; ₹2 700 cr capex plan for specialty steel.
  • Jul 2026: Aluminium foil plant commissioned; 1.5 MTPA beneficiation unit operational.
  • Oct 2026: ₹50 000 cr greenfield steel complex MoU; acquisition of 170 MT coal block (Phutamura).

What moves this stock

  • Capacity‑expansion announcements (cold‑rolling, aluminium, beneficiation) trigger strong upside.
  • Entry into new product lines or segments (roofing, wagon, stainless steel) is rewarded with price jumps.
  • Large government‑linked projects or mining‑rights wins (Maharashtra steel complex, coal block) produce the biggest rallies.

Overall, Shyam Metalics’ share price has been a function of how aggressively the company signals growth‑driving projects; absent clear news, price moves remain unexplained.

522249.one: Re‑rated from Rs 453.5 to Rs 882.2 as export‑led profit surges and dividend news lifted the stock, while a few unexplained dips kept volatility high.
522249.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 02 Feb 2026 – “Mayur Uniquoters expects strong export growth to outpace domestic expansion.”
    Price reaction: 4‑week rally from ₹477.9 to ₹575.45 (+20%).
  • 21 May 2026 – “Mayur Uniquoters PAT rises 73% in Q4 FY26.”
    Price reaction: 4‑week rally from ₹549.25 to ₹754.45 (+37%).
  • 27 May 2026 – “Q4 2026 earnings call highlights robust profit growth.”
    Price reaction: Reinforced the May rally, keeping the stock above ₹730.
  • 06‑07 Aug 2026 – “Share price gains 1.25% after Q1 FY27 results; record profit surge.”
    Price reaction: Small but positive intraday bump, confirming the upward bias.
  • 04‑07 Nov 2026 – “Q2 FY27 results: revenue +18% YoY, PAT +42% YoY; ₹300 cr export OEM revenue target.”
    Price reaction: Stabilised the stock around ₹745 after the June peak.

De‑rating factors

  • 27 Jan 2025 → 24 Feb 2025 – No headline.
    Price reaction: 4‑week fall from ₹547.6 to ₹468.55 (‑14%).
  • 14 Jul 2025 → 11 Aug 2025 – No headline.
    Price reaction: 4‑week fall from ₹618.1 to ₹517.25 (‑16%).
  • 28 Apr 2025 → 26 May 2025 – No headline.
    Price reaction: 4‑week rise from ₹453.5 to ₹587.05 (+29%) but the low base suggests earlier weakness not captured by headlines.

Pivots & turning points

  • 22 Sep 2025 – Re‑appointment of MD & CEO Suresh Kumar Poddar (leadership continuity).
  • 14 Jul 2026 – Resignation of senior manager (potential operational impact).
  • 20 Aug 2026 – ₹6 per share dividend proposal (cash return signal).
  • 04 Nov 2026 – Promoter Kiran Poddar increases stake & solar‑project approval (strategic diversification).

What moves this stock

  • Export outlook: Positive export guidance (Feb 2026) triggers sizable rallies.
  • Profit & PAT surprises: Large year‑on‑year PAT jumps (May 2026, Q2 FY27) produce strong upside.
  • Dividend/return announcements: Dividend proposals and promoter stake increases give the market a tangible reward cue.

Overall, Mayur Uniquoters’ price action over the past two years is most responsive to export‑growth expectations, sharp profit beats, and cash‑return news; unexplained dips remain a reminder of underlying market noise.

543398.one: *De‑rated from Rs 496 to Rs 205 as early‑FY growth fizzled, negative analyst ratings and executive‑share concerns outweighed occasional earnings‑driven rallies.*
543398.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Oct 24 2025 – Q2 FY25 results: Profit up 17.2% YoY, revenue +34.2%; stock jumped from ~₹428 to ₹489 (+14%) by Nov 10 2025.
  • Feb 02 2026 – Q3 FY26 profit up 19% YoY: Shares rallied ≈8% on the day.
  • Apr 02 2026 – Healtheon AI deal & SocGen stake: $3 m investment and a 0.5 % SocGen purchase sparked a ≈20% surge (single‑day volume record on Apr 3).

De‑rating factors

  • Dec 22 2025 – Jan 19 2026: Stock fell ‑15% (₹461 → ₹392). The dip coincided with news that top‑executive Adugudi Venkatraman’s holdings lost 4.5 % of value (Dec 25 2025).
  • Oct 12 2026 – Nov 06 2026: Price slid ‑16% (₹243 → ₹205) as the stock was rated “Sell” (Oct 14) and flagged as near an all‑time low (Oct 22).
  • Feb 02 2026 – Mar 02 2026: Despite a profit boost, the share price dropped ‑29% (₹427 → ₹305). No headline directly aligns, so the cause isn’t clear from the available news.

Pivots & turning points

  • Jul 15 2026 – New CEO Sonal Ramrakhiani: Signalled a shift toward AI‑driven growth and $200 m revenue target.
  • Jul 01 2026 – Delay in Decision Point acquisition: Highlighted integration risk.
  • Aug 17 2026 – ESG rating of 77: First independent sustainability score, potentially broadening investor base.

What moves this stock

  • Earnings beats & profit acceleration (e.g., Q2 FY25, Q3 FY26) trigger short‑term rallies.
  • Strategic partnerships / capital infusions (Healtheon AI deal, SocGen stake) produce sharp upside.
  • Analyst downgrades, executive‑share sell‑offs, and rating “Sell” signals generate pronounced downside pressure.

540724.one: *De‑rated from Rs 1094.5 to Rs 1032.3 as ownership turbulence and margin pressure outweighed short‑term earnings lifts.*
540724.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 31 Dec 2024 – Competition watchdog clears majority‑stake sale – the approval sparked a +12 % 4‑week rally (₹1 022.85 → ₹1 150.6).
  • 28 Apr 2026 – Q4 FY26 profit & 319 % EBITDA jump, Rs 0.50 dividend – the turnaround lifted the stock in the May‑Jun 2026 window, contributing to a +16 % rise (₹980.1 → ₹1 135.7).
  • 07 Jan 2026 – Motilal Oswal initiates “Buy” coverage – the broker’s endorsement helped sustain the post‑April rally, keeping the price above the FY26 low.

De‑rating factors

  • 29 Jul 2025 – Madhusudan Kela family sells down its Prataap stake – the sell‑off coincided with a ‑15 % 4‑week slide (₹1 070.7 → ₹907.6).
  • 10 Feb 2026 – Q3 FY27 results show margin compression from input‑cost inflation – the earnings miss triggered a ‑16 % dip (₹1 077.5 → ₹908).
  • 27 Jan 2025 – Q3 loss widens – the loss announcement pushed the share ‑4 % on the day and fed into the early‑2025 weakness.

Pivots & turning points

  • Jan 2025 – Competition regulator approves majority takeover (ownership change).
  • Apr 2026 – Return to profit and aggressive quick‑commerce push (new growth engine).
  • Aug 2026 – Chairman Arvind Kumar Mehta resigns; ESAR grants to employees (governance shift).
  • Oct 2026 – Plans for a new Indore manufacturing facility (capacity expansion).

What moves this stock

  • Ownership news – take‑over approvals, stake sales or purchases by promoters or large investors swing the price sharply.
  • Earnings & margin updates – profit turn‑arounds lift the stock; cost‑inflation‑driven losses pull it down.
  • Regulatory & policy events – competition‑watchdog clearances, GST rate changes, and broker rating upgrades act as catalysts.

543270.html:
One‑line story: From ₹1,618 in Nov 2024 to ₹5,449 in Nov 2026, MTAR Tech was re‑rated on a cascade of mega‑order wins and record earnings, then de‑rated by an insider‑trading scandal and profit‑taking after a stellar Q2 FY27 release.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Order win & Q2 FY25 growth – Dec 20 2024 the company disclosed Rs 226 cr of clean‑energy and aerospace orders; Q2 FY25 results (Oct 2024) showed 48 % QoQ revenue rise and 122 % EBITDA jump.
  • Sep 2025 – Oct 2025: Mega clean‑energy orders – Sep 10 2025 a Rs 386 cr order from Bloom Energy was announced; Oct 15 2025 an additional Rs 67 cr order was disclosed. The stock surged 38 % (1408 → 1936) then 29 % (1880 → 2419).
  • Jan 2026 – Apr 2026: Record Q3 FY26 earnings & guidance lift – Jan 30 2026 Q3 FY26 results posted a 117 % YoY profit rise and a Rs 1,368 cr order inflow; a Dec 15 2025 amendment added Rs 370 cr of orders. The share jumped 52 % (2400 → 3658) and then 81 % (3576 → 6457).
  • Jun 2026 – Jul 2026: Compliance blow‑up – Feb 7 2026 the firm reported a second insider‑trading violation (profit of ₹1,252 disgorged). The market trimmed the rally, pulling the price 28 % down from the June 15 high of ₹8,375 to ₹6,046.
  • Oct 2026 – Nov 2026: Profit‑taking after Q2 FY27 – Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) delivered record Rs 406 cr revenue and 483 % EBITDA growth, yet the stock fell 30 % (₹7,782 → ₹5,449) as investors booked gains.

What re‑rated it

  • Rs 226 cr order win (Dec 2024) in clean‑energy & aerospace.
  • Rs 386 cr Bloom Energy order (Sep 2025) and Rs 67 cr follow‑on order (Oct 2025).
  • Rs 370 cr order amendment (Dec 2025) boosting the order book to >₹800 cr.
  • Q3 FY26 earnings: profit up 117 % YoY, revenue +59 % YoY, order inflow Rs 1,368 cr.
  • Revised FY26 revenue guidance to 30‑35 % growth (Nov 2025).
  • Q2 FY27 record revenue (Rs 406 cr) and EBITDA margin 24.4 % (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Insider‑trading policy violation disclosed Feb 2026 (profit disgorgement).
  • Sharp profit‑taking after the Q2 FY27 beat (Oct‑Nov 2026).

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of large defence or clean‑energy contracts (e.g., Bloom Energy, nuclear reactor bids).
  • Updates on order‑book conversion, especially civil‑nuclear projects or LCA Tejas volume orders.
  • Milestones in capacity expansion – fuel‑cell Phase 2/3 commissioning or new manufacturing facilities.
543270.sources: mtar.in corporate announcements, Business Standard (Q3 FY26 report), ScoutQuest (Q2 FY27 call), ScanX (insider‑trading violation), StockScans (Q2 FY27 price reaction).

532843.html:
One‑line story: Fortis Healthcare swung from Rs 620.75 to Rs 766.9 – a net‑up‑trend +23% – as strong earnings, capacity‑additions and IHH’s stake‑boost re‑rated it, then a Delhi High Court forensic‑audit order and a modest Q2 FY27 profit dip de‑rated it.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Q2 FY25 lift & new chair” – Q2 FY25 profit +5% and 12% revenue growth (Nov 8) plus a Rs 1,550 cr NCD raise and a 31% stake‑consolidation in Agilus; share rose from 620.75 to 714.25 (+15%). New chairman Leo Puri appointed (Dec 27) and the stock slipped to 626.85 by Jan 27 (‑14%).
  • May 2025 – Oct 2025: “FY25 earnings surge & IHH stake approval” – Q4 FY25 profit dip but revenue +12.4% and a 1,000‑bed capacity plan (May 21) lifted the price from 664.70 to 763.30 (+15%). IHH’s SEBI‑cleared plan to increase its Fortis holding (July 2025) and the regulator‑clearance of the long‑delayed takeover (Oct 6) drove the stock to a 2‑year high of 1,084.9 on Oct 13 (+17%).
  • Feb 2026 – Jun 2026: “FY26 momentum” – Q3 FY26 results (Feb 13) showed revenue up 14.8% and profit +84% (share at 929 in Aug 2026). Q4 FY26 PAT +44% and revenue +17.8% (May 23) pushed the price from 788.75 to 922.95 (+17%).
  • Aug 2026 – Oct 2026: “Forensic‑audit shock” – Delhi High Court ordered a six‑month forensic audit of historic Daiichi‑Fortis transactions (Aug 31). The legal cloud sent the share down from 886 to 736.5 (‑17%).
  • Nov 2026: “Cautious Q2 FY27” – Q2 FY27 profit fell 3% while revenue rose 17% (Nov 5); management flagged the audit but stayed upbeat. The stock settled around 766.9 by Nov 6.

What re‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 earnings beat and 12% revenue rise.
  • Aggressive capacity‑add plan (+700 beds) and Agilus stake consolidation.
  • IHH’s SEBI‑cleared increase to a 31% indirect holding and regulator‑approved takeover clearance (Oct 2025).
  • FY26 Q4 profit surge (+44%) and 17% revenue growth.

What de‑rated it

  • Delhi High Court’s six‑month forensic‑audit order (Aug 2026).
  • Q2 FY27 profit dip (‑3%) despite revenue growth, reinforcing legal uncertainty.

News that moves this stock

  • Any court order or regulatory decision on the Daiichi‑Fortis forensic audit.
  • SEBI/stock‑exchange approvals for IHH’s stake‑increase or open‑offer actions.
  • Announcements of large capacity‑expansion projects or major acquisitions (e.g., new super‑specialty hospitals).
532843.sources: Business Standard, The Hindu Business Line, Reuters, Moneycontrol, CNBC TV18.
