500257.one: Lupin was re‑rated from Rs 2104 to Rs 1997 as a “growth‑driven” generic player, then de‑rated by US pricing pressure and product competition, ending a round‑trip swing of ≈ 5 % over two years.
500257.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Jan 2025: “Profit‑beat rally, then US pricing shock” – Q2 FY25 profit beat (74 % YoY) lifted the stock to a 2369 peak; a week later US pricing‑erosion worries and Tolvaptan competition knocked it down 13 % to 2056.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: “Q3 FY25 results and ANDA surge” – Strong Q3 FY25 earnings (PAT + 39 %) and six new US ANDA approvals drove the price up to 2201, then a modest pull‑back to 2037 as the market priced in emerging‑market slowdown.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: “US pricing erosion bites” – Commentary on US price erosion and tighter margins for legacy products pushed the share to a low of 1918.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: “Domestic momentum steadies” – Robust India sales and new diabetes launches steadied the stock, lifting it to 1972.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “US revenue stabilises” – Management said US revenue would settle at $250 m per quarter; the reassurance lifted the price to 2174.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: “US guidance upgrade & Amifampridine win” – FY27 US sales guidance raised to $1.1‑$1.2 bn and USFDA approval for Amifampridine tablets sent the stock soaring to a 2379 high.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: “Regulatory wins & leadership change” – FDA nod for Phytonadione injectable and appointment of Brian Savage as President‑CLO gave a modest lift, but concerns over Tolvaptan competition kept the price near 2364.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “Mixed Q2 FY27, US pricing pressure returns” – Q2 FY27 showed steady organic growth but US pricing pressure on Tolvaptan and a USFDA Diclofenac approval caused a dip to 1988; a small rebound to 1997 followed the earnings call.

What re‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 profit beat (Nov 2024).
  • Q3 FY25 earnings beat and six new US ANDA approvals (Feb 2025).
  • US revenue stabilisation guidance ($250 m/quarter) (May 2025).
  • FY27 US sales guidance lift and Amifampridine FDA approval (Aug 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • US pricing erosion on legacy generics and Tolvaptan competition (May 2025 & Aug 2026).
  • USFDA observations on the Pithampur plant (Sep 2024) that lingered in market sentiment.

News that moves this stock

  • Any USFDA approval for complex generics or biosimilars (especially in high‑margin therapeutic areas).
  • Updates on US pricing reforms, patent litigation outcomes, or major price‑erosion announcements.
  • Large domestic order wins or new product launches in India’s diabetes/insulin franchise.
500257.sources: Reuters, Business Standard, CNBC TV18, Lupin press releases, Moneycontrol.

531209.one: De‑rated from ₹1,204.55 (Nov 2024) to ₹631.65 (Nov 2026) as profit fell sharply and margins were squeezed by rising AI‑talent costs, despite occasional revenue‑growth spikes that briefly re‑rated the stock.
531209.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Jan 2025: “Profit‑drift after Q3 FY 24‑25” – Q3 results showed PAT down 15% YoY; the share slipped from ₹1,204.55 to ₹907 by Feb 2025.
  • Apr 2025 – May 2025: “FY 24‑25 beat and AI‑first push” – FY results posted PAT ₹163 cr, EPS ₹61.4 and a clear AI‑led roadmap; the stock surged 45% to a high of ₹1,282.15 on 26 May 2025.
  • Jun 2025 – Aug 2025: “Q1 FY 25‑26 growth, but margin worries” – Q1 showed revenue ₹217 cr but management warned of higher AI‑talent spend; the price fell 15% to ₹1,015.7 by 28 Jul 2025, then steadied around ₹998.
  • Sep 2025 – Feb 2026: “FY 25‑26 profit compression” – Q4 FY 25‑26 PAT halved to ₹34.55 cr; investors punished the margin drop, pushing the stock to ₹915.6 in Feb 2026 and then to ₹817.05 by 4 May 2026.
  • Mar 2026 – Nov 2026: “Q3 FY 25‑26 slump and Q2 FY 27 margin squeeze” – Q3 FY 25‑26 PAT fell to ₹20.7 cr; Q2 FY 27 showed revenue up 8% but profit down 19% and AI‑staff costs eroding EBITDA. The share slid to ₹698.25 in Aug 2026 and hit a low of ₹628.65 on 2 Nov 2026, trading at ₹631.65 today.

What re‑rated it

  • FY 24‑25 results beating expectations (PAT ₹163 cr, EPS ₹61.4).
  • Announcement of AI‑first product roadmap and AI‑enhanced FinnOne Neo/Axia upgrades.
  • Order‑book crossing the ₹1,000 cr mark in FY 25‑26, signalling strong pipeline.
  • Strategic partnership with FPT to launch FinnOne Neo 9.0 in Vietnam (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Q3 FY 24‑25 profit decline (PAT ₹35 cr vs ₹41 cr YoY).
  • Q3 FY 25‑26 profit slump (PAT ₹20.7 cr, EPS ₹7.86).
  • Q4 FY 25‑26 margin compression (PAT ₹34.55 cr, EPS ₹13.12) and guidance of higher AI‑talent spend.
  • Q2 FY 27 margin pressure from rising employee and AI‑skill costs despite revenue growth.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of a multi‑billion‑rupee digital‑lending contract with a major Indian or global bank.
  • Launch of a next‑generation AI‑driven version of FinnOne Neo or FinnAxia (e.g., FinnOne Neo 10.0).
  • Order‑book milestone crossing ₹1,500 cr or a significant increase in the proportion of product‑only revenue.
531209.sources: The Hindu BusinessLine, Nucleus Software press releases (nucleussoftware.com), CNBC TV18, MarketsMojo, ScoutQuest (crisp.scoutquest.in)

500472.one: From Rs 5,084 (Nov 2024) to Rs 1,445 (Nov 2026) the stock was first de‑rated on weak FY25 Q2 results, then re‑rated on Q4 earnings, rail‑way orders and a new Vertevo brand, before a de‑rating wave from the Oct 2025 demerger and margin pressure drove it to a two‑year low.
500472.html:
How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Jan 2025: Muted FY25 Q2 results – Revenue grew 10 % YoY but EBITDA margin fell 84 bps; PAT rose only 4.6 % YoY. The stock slid 7 % to a six‑month low and kept falling to Rs 4,255 by mid‑Jan.
Jan 2025 – May 2025: Profit‑slide & modest recovery – Q3 PAT fell 17 % YoY to Rs 110 cr, pulling the price down to Rs 3,927 (‑13 % in four weeks). A DMRC refurbishment tender (₹6.7 cr) and the May 16 Q4 results (PAT +20 % YoY, revenue flat) sparked a 9 % jump, lifting the share to Rs 4,493 by early May and further to Rs 4,493 → Rs 4,693 by late May (+20 % in four weeks).
May 2025 – Nov 2025: Demerger shock – The Oct 1 2025 announcement that SKF India would split into Automotive and Industrial entities (listing of the industrial arm expected Nov 2025) sent the stock tumbling 57 % to Rs 2,078 by early Nov.
Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Stabilisation – A November 6 2025 rail‑freight contract (₹42 cr) and the launch of the SKF Vertevo brand (Nov 4 2026 investor deck) steadied the price at Rs 1,752.
Feb 2026 – Nov 2026: Gradual erosion – Q2 FY27 (Nov 6 2026) showed strong YoY revenue but margin compression from a timing gap in passing raw‑material cost inflation; the share slipped to a 2‑year low of Rs 1,395 (Oct 26 2026) before edging back to Rs 1,445.

What re‑rated it

  • Q4 FY25 PAT up 20 % YoY and revenue beat (May 2025).
  • Large rail‑freight bearing order (₹42 cr, Nov 2025).
  • DMRC axle‑bearing refurbishment award (₹6.7 cr, Apr 2025).
  • Launch of the high‑margin “Vertevo” brand (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 muted earnings and margin squeeze (Nov 2024).
  • Q3 FY25 PAT decline 17 % YoY (Feb 2025).
  • Oct 2025 demerger announcement splitting automotive and industrial businesses.
  • Q2 FY27 margin compression from raw‑material cost timing gap.

News that moves this stock

  • New railway or metro‑rail bearing contracts (especially freight‑roller or CTRB awards).
  • Progress on the demerger integration and listing of the industrial entity.
  • Updates on raw‑material price trends and SKF’s pricing pass‑through strategy.
500472.sources: Business Standard, SKF press releases (Oct 2025 demerger, Nov 2026 Vertevo launch), Rail Analysis India (Nov 2025 rail contract), Alpha Spread (Feb 2025 Q1 earnings call), Delhi Metro tender notice (Apr 2025).

543325.one: Rolex Rings was sharply de‑rated from ₹206 to ₹114 (‑45 %) between Nov 2024 and Nov 2025 on earnings weakness, a Rs 227 cr Right‑of‑Recompense demand and a 45 % PAT plunge, then re‑rated to ₹212 (+86 %) by Nov 2026 after a record Q2 FY27 driven by auto‑component demand, margin expansion and a one‑off tariff refund.
543325.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Mixed Q2 FY25 results → demand‑notice shock” – Q2 FY25 showed a 7.5 % revenue dip but a modest 4.9 % profit rise; the market stayed upbeat (price ≈ ₹206). On 5 Feb 2025 the company received a Rs 227.86 cr Right‑of‑Recompense demand from Union Bank, sparking a sell‑off to ₹169.99.

  • Feb 2025 – Nov 2025: “Earnings pain and legal cloud” – Dec 2025 Q3 FY25 disclosed a 45 % YoY PAT fall to ₹201 mn and an extraordinary provision, pushing the stock to a low of ₹126.22 (May 2025). A CARE rating note (Aug 2025) highlighted the RoR liability, and the lingering legal risk dragged the price further down to ₹114.17 (Nov 2025).

  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Early FY26 recovery” – Q1 FY26 results (released early 2026) showed revenue rebound to ₹3,108 cr, EBITDA margin improvement to 24 % and a stronger order‑book, lifting the share to ₹125.71.

  • Feb 2026 – Nov 2026: “Momentum from auto‑components and margin upside” – Q2 FY26 (mid‑2026) reported robust auto‑component growth, gross‑margin lift of ~700 bps and a one‑off US tariff refund, sending the price to ₹150.84 (May 2026) and then modestly higher to ₹156.68 (Aug 2026).

  • Nov 2026: “Record Q2 FY27 – full re‑rating” – Investor deck (4 Nov 2026) and earnings call (6 Nov 2026) announced the strongest quarter ever: revenue ₹389 cr (+43 % YoY), EBITDA ₹94 cr (+72 % YoY), PAT ₹74 cr (+68 % YoY) and EBITDA margin 24.2 %. The market surged to ₹201.17 and closed at ₹212.16.

What re‑rated it

  • Record Q2 FY27 revenue (+43 % YoY) and profit (+68 % YoY).
  • Auto‑components now 54 % of sales, delivering higher‑margin mix.
  • One‑off US tariff refund (~₹18 cr) boosting top‑line and margins.
  • Strong order‑book (₹120‑₹125 cr / month) and capacity utilisation rising to ~70 %.

What de‑rated it

  • 45 % YoY PAT decline in Q3 FY25 plus extraordinary provision.
  • Rs 227 cr Right‑of‑Recompense demand notice and ongoing legal dispute.
  • Margin pressure from higher raw‑material costs and ocean‑freight spikes (early FY25).

News that moves this stock

  • Large auto‑component orders or new program launches (especially from US/EU OEMs).
  • Resolution of the Right‑of‑Recompense liability (settlement or court outcome).
  • US tariff policy changes or additional duty refunds affecting the one‑off revenue boost.
543325.sources: Business Standard, Quartr, AlphaStreet, CARE Ratings, Business Upturn.

543350.html:
Story in one line: From Rs 1,119 to Rs 1,467 – Vijaya Diagnostic was de‑rated by leadership changes and regulatory hiccups, then re‑rated by a string of high‑growth earnings, aggressive hub roll‑outs and margin‑boosting AI/technology upgrades.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025 : Earnings boost – Q2 FY25 posted 31.8 % YoY revenue growth, strong volume and margin expansion; the stock climbed to Rs 1,134.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025 : Recovery after modest Q4 FY25 – FY25 Q4 showed 11.6 % revenue rise and six new hubs; the price fell to Rs 993 then rebounded to Rs 1,055 as the network rollout gained traction.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026 : Growth slowdown – FY26 Q1‑Q2 results signaled slower volume growth and higher hub‑capex, pulling the share down to a low of Rs 965.
  • May 2026 – Nov 2026 : Re‑rating wave – Q4 FY26 delivered 26.6 % revenue jump, EBITDA margin up to 43.5 % and a flagship Bengaluru hub; the stock surged 30 % to Rs 1,279, then climbed further on Q1 FY27 (22.8 % revenue growth, AI‑driven diagnostics) and Q2 FY27 (26.7 % revenue growth, 350 bps EBITDA margin expansion) reaching Rs 1,469.

What re‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 earnings beat – 31.8 % revenue growth, 23 % PAT rise and 22 bps EBITDA margin lift.
  • FY25 Q4 hub expansion – launch of six new hubs (Bengaluru, Pune, West Bengal) and 11.6 % revenue increase.
  • Q4 FY26 performance – 26.6 % revenue surge, EBITDA margin 43.5 % and the 10,000 sq ft flagship hub in JP Nagar, Bengaluru.
  • Q1 FY27 growth – 22.8 % YoY revenue rise, 16.5 % volume growth, AI‑enabled CT reporting and new spokes in Hyderabad & AP.
  • Q2 FY27 momentum – 26.7 % YoY revenue growth, 16.5 % volume gain, 350 bps EBITDA margin expansion, acquisition of Arya Wellness in Guwahati and rollout of genomic testing.

What de‑rated it

  • COO resignation (Nov 2024) – leadership change sparked a 14 % four‑week sell‑off.
  • Regulatory fine for a prenatal‑test error (May 2025) – 2.2  lakh fine and negative press triggered a 13 % drop.
  • FY25‑26 growth slowdown (Jan‑Feb 2025 & Apr‑May 2025) – muted Q4‑FY25 guidance and higher hub‑cost expectations drove 16 % and 13 % four‑week declines.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of new hub or spoke openings, especially in Tier‑2/3 cities (e.g., Bengaluru, Hyderabad, West Bengal).
  • Regulatory approvals or setbacks for advanced imaging/AI diagnostics (wide‑bore 3T MRI, AI‑driven CT reporting).
  • Strategic acquisitions or partnerships (e.g., Arya Wellness Centre, other regional diagnostic chains).
543350.sources: Business Standard, Indian Pharma Post, Medical Buyer, BSE filings, Indian Pharma Post (Q4 FY25), Indian Pharma Post (Q4 FY26), Concall PDF (Q1 FY27), Marketscreener (Q2 FY27).

542665.one: Neogen Chemicals swung from Rs 2121 → Rs 2629 as fire‑related setbacks de‑rated the stock (Nov 2024‑Dec 2025) and a cascade of insurance recoveries, rating upgrades, battery‑chemistry scale‑up and the GPCB clearance re‑rated it (Feb 2026‑Nov 2026).
542665.html:
How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – May 2025: Fire‑hit Dahej & FY25 guidance cut – March 2025 fire crippled the Dahej plant; FY25 results (May 2025) highlighted the loss, a Rs 14 cr exceptional item and a revised FY26 revenue target of Rs 775‑850 cr (down from Rs 950‑1 000 cr). Share price fell from Rs 2121 to Rs 1491.

May 2025 – Nov 2025: Resilience & modest rebound – Q3 FY25 (Feb 2025) showed 22 % revenue growth and strong BuLi Chem integration; Q4 FY25 (May 2025) still noted fire impact but delivered 13 % FY25 revenue growth. Stock edged up to Rs 1452.

Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Guidance downgrade & lingering fire concerns – Investors digested the FY26 guidance cut and ongoing plant outage, driving the stock to a low of Rs 1055 on 1 Dec 2025.

Feb 2026 – May 2026: Insurance recoveries & rating uplift – Q1 FY26 (Aug 2025) reported insurance claim receipts of Rs 80 cr and a stable credit rating; CRISIL removed the rating‑watch in Aug 2025. The share rallied to Rs 1772.

May 2026 – Nov 2026: Battery‑chemistry boom & regulatory green‑light – Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) delivered 42 % revenue growth, 51 % EBITDA rise and a 144 % PAT jump, powered by Neogen Ionics scaling to Rs 37 cr. The GPCB revoked fire‑related restrictions on the Dahej plant (Nov 8 2026), unlocking full operations. A 600 cr QIP was oversubscribed 6.5× and the long‑term rating outlook turned to “A‑/Stable”. Stock surged to a 2‑year high of Rs 2629.

What re‑rated it

  • GPCB revocation of Dahej fire restrictions (full plant restart).
  • Q2 FY27 results: 42 % top‑line, 51 % EBITDA growth, battery‑chemistry revenue up 10× YoY.
  • 600 cr QIP oversubscribed 6.5×, de‑leveraging balance sheet.
  • CRISIL rating outlook upgrade to “A‑/Stable”.
  • Organolithium capacity expansion adding ~Rs 150‑200 cr revenue potential.

What de‑rated it

  • March 2025 Dahej fire causing plant shutdown and a Rs 14 cr exceptional loss.
  • FY26 revenue guidance cut (Rs 775‑850 cr vs. prior Rs 950‑1 000 cr).
  • Soft pricing across specialty chemicals dragging margins.

News that moves this stock

  • Final clearance and commercial commissioning of the Dahej battery‑materials plant.
  • Signed long‑term supply contracts with domestic EV battery manufacturers.
  • Further rating outlook changes or major debt‑restructuring announcements.
542665.sources: Neogen Chemicals press releases (Nov 2024‑Nov 2026), BSE filings, CRISIL rating updates, market commentary (Investing.com, TipRanks).

543996.one: Updater Services Ltd. re‑rated from Rs 406.65 to Rs 200.38 as earnings beat expectations but later de‑rated when guidance cuts and margin pressure hit, with the stock swinging between Rs 155.88 and Rs 210.03.
543996.html:
How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Q4 FY24 results (Sep 2024) showed a 182.9 % jump in net profit and 13.3 % sales growth, yet the share fell 14 % to Rs 346.85 as the market priced in a slower growth outlook.
Feb 2025 – May 2025: Q1 FY25 (Mar 2025) delivered 33.3 % profit growth and 12 % sales rise, but the price slid another 18 % to Rs 283.45 amid concerns over BSS margin compression.
May 2025 – Aug 2025: Q2 FY25 (Jun 2025) posted modest 12.7 % profit lift and 7.4 % sales rise; the share dipped 7 % to Rs 263.15 as investors questioned cost‑control.
Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: Q3 FY25 (Dec 2025) saw net profit plunge 70 % YoY, dragging the price down 23 % to Rs 201.29.
Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Motilal Oswal’s Nov 7 2025 downgrade to “Neutral” and a 12 % cut in FY26 earnings estimates pushed the share 22 % lower to Rs 155.88.
Feb 2026 – May 2026: Q1 FY26 (Jun 2026) modest 3.9 % profit rise and 9.1 % sales growth lifted the stock 14 % to Rs 177.
May 2026 – Aug 2026: Q2 FY26 (Sep 2026) net profit surged 62 % YoY, lifting the share 18 % to Rs 210.03.
Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Q3 FY26 (Dec 2026) profit jumped 62 % YoY, yet the price slipped 3 % to Rs 204.12, settling at Rs 200.38 on Nov 8 2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Strong quarterly earnings growth (Q4 FY24, Q2 FY26).
  • 62 % YoY profit lift in Q2 FY26, signalling margin recovery.
  • SIS’s 4.2 % stake acquisition in Feb 2026, boosting investor confidence.

What de‑rated it

  • Motilal Oswal’s Nov 2025 downgrade and earnings estimate cuts.
  • Persistent margin pressure in the BSS segment.
  • Q3 FY25 profit collapse and subsequent guidance cuts.

News that moves this stock

  • Large BSS order wins or cancellations.
  • IFM margin improvement announcements.
  • Regulatory approvals or changes affecting service contracts.
  • Significant stake acquisitions or divestments by major shareholders.
543996.sources: Business Standard, Capital Market News, MarketScreener, NDTV Profit, Livemint.

500877.one: Apollo Tyres went from Rs 491 → Rs 416 in two years, first re‑rated on strong revenue‑plus‑pricing news (Nov 2024‑Mar 2025) and later de‑rated as raw‑material cost spikes and weak OEM demand ate margins (Dec 2024‑Jun 2026), with a brief re‑rating bounce after Q2 FY27 revenue‑growth guidance (Nov 2026).
500877.html:
How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Mar 2025: Revenue‑plus‑pricing lift – H1 FY25 showed 3 % top‑line growth, strong replacement‑segment sales in India and premium‑mix gains in Europe; the market pushed the share from 491.05 → 547.8 (+15 %).

Dec 2024 – Jan 2025: OEM‑demand & raw‑material drag – Management warned of a “weak OEM segment in India” and a 15 % rise in rubber costs; the stock slid 540.7 → 423.4 (‑22 %).

Feb – Mar 2025: Cost‑stabilisation & capacity add‑on – Q3 FY25 (Feb 6) beat revenue estimates, announced 2‑3 % price hikes and a ~10 % PCR capacity boost; raw‑material cost outlook softened. The share rebounded 374.3 → 426.05 (+14 %).

Apr 2025: Dividend & premium‑mix focus – Q4 FY25 (May 15) confirmed a Rs 5 per‑share dividend and continued UHP‑tyre mix expansion; investors rewarded the cash return and the capacity plan, lifting the price 407.95 → 476.5 (+17 %).

Feb – Jun 2026: Margin squeeze – Q2 FY27 (Nov 6 2026) flagged “raw‑material cost pressures and margin compression” despite revenue growth; the market punished the stock 489.65 → 400.3 (‑18 %).

May – Jun 2026: Revenue‑growth bounce – The same quarter’s 16.6 % YoY revenue rise and pricing actions sparked a recovery 371.8 → 425.5 (+14 %).

What re‑rated it

  • H1 FY25 revenue beat and strong replacement‑segment growth (Nov 2024).
  • Q3 FY25 price‑hike announcement and ~10 % PCR capacity expansion plan (Feb 2025).
  • Dividend declaration and premium‑mix (UHP) push in Q4 FY25 (May 2025).
  • Q2 FY27 16.6 % YoY revenue growth and pricing actions (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • 15 % jump in rubber/raw‑material costs and weak OEM demand (Dec 2024).
  • Margin compression and higher material expense highlighted in Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026).

News that moves this stock

  • Raw‑material price shocks (rubber, oil) or cost‑containment measures.
  • Capacity‑expansion or plant‑shutdown updates (e.g., PCR or European plant pivots).
  • Major OEM order wins or losses in India/Europe, especially for CV and passenger‑car tyres.
500877.sources: Tyrepress, Reuters, CNBC TV18, Economic Times (ETAuto), Livemint.

544455.one: GNG Electronics raced from Rs 312.5 to Rs 547.5 (‑23% from its 2‑yr high) as a blockbuster IPO, record‑breaking FY‑26 results and a “best‑ever” Q2 FY‑27 lifted the stock, while profit‑taking and higher tax‑rate worries trimmed the rally.
544455.html:
How the story unfolded

Jul 2025 – Oct 2025: IPO debut & early hype – Listing at a 50 % premium (Rs 355) sparked a jump to Rs 334.9.
Dec 2025 – Jan 2026: Market correction – After the post‑IPO euphoria faded, the share slid 20 % to Rs 252, the lowest point of the period.
Jan 2026 – Apr 2026: FY‑26 Q4 beat & financing boost – Strong Q4 FY‑26 results (₹1.32 bn net profit) and a supplemental ₹800 cr working‑capital facility lifted the price 66 % to Rs 424.6.
Apr 2026 – Jul 2026: FY‑27 Q1 momentum – Q1 FY27 revenue up 32 % and margin expansion drove the stock 24 % higher to Rs 528.7.
Oct 2026 – Nov 2026: FY‑27 Q2 “best‑ever” quarter – Q2 FY27 revenue +42 % and EBITDA doubled, prompting a 34 % surge to a 2‑yr high of Rs 708.1 (Oct 12). Profit‑taking and tax‑rate concerns then pulled the price back 23 % to Rs 547.5 (Nov 9).

What re‑rated it

  • Blockbuster IPO with 150× oversubscription and 50 % premium.
  • FY‑26 Q4 earnings: net profit more than doubled, EPS up to ₹3.70, and guidance lift.
  • FY‑27 Q1 results: 32 % revenue growth, 329 bps margin expansion, upgraded FY‑27 guidance.
  • FY‑27 Q2 “best‑ever” quarter: 42 % revenue jump, EBITDA up 100 %, full‑year outlook raised to 40 % top‑line growth.
  • Brand‑building initiatives (Electronics Bazaar marketing, Technical Guruji partnership) improving pricing power.

What de‑rated it

  • Profit‑taking after the Oct 12 peak despite strong fundamentals.
  • Announcement of a higher effective tax rate (≈ 15 %) for FY‑27, tempering net‑profit expectations.
  • Elevated inventory build‑up flagged as a working‑capital risk in analyst Q&A.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of large corporate or government refurbishment contracts (e.g., bulk e‑waste buy‑backs).
  • Regulatory changes affecting e‑waste standards or minimum public‑shareholding requirements.
  • Major capacity expansion or new brand‑partner launches that broaden the Electronics Bazaar footprint.
544455.sources: Economic Times, Business Standard, Investing.com, MarketScreener, Innovacia.

509675.html:
BirlaNu Ltd (BIRLANU.NS) – One‑Line Story
Re‑rated from ₹2,462 to ₹1,229 because Parador’s persistent losses and weak European demand dragged the stock, while strong Indian growth, Clean Coats acquisition and new capacity at Nellore lifted it back.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Q4 FY25 earnings call shows double‑digit India growth but Parador losses; shares fall 21 % to ₹1,858.8.
  • Apr 2025 – May 2025: Q1 FY26 earnings call highlights 76 % Pipes volume growth, 23 % Construction Chemicals revenue, and Clean Coats acquisition; shares rise 28 % to ₹2,343.6.
  • Jul 2025 – Aug 2025: Q2 FY26 earnings call reports weak Parador demand and price pressure; shares drop 18 % to ₹1,934.
  • Oct 2025 – Nov 2025: Q3 FY26 earnings call shows continued Parador losses, India business strong; shares fall to ₹1,764.1.
  • Jan 2026 – Mar 2026: Q4 FY26 earnings call confirms India double‑digit growth, Parador losses; shares edge up 1 % to ₹1,781.5.
  • Apr 2026 – Jun 2026: Q1 FY27 earnings call announces a ₹90 crore provision for Parador and ongoing losses; shares plunge 27 % to ₹1,303.5.
  • Jul 2026 – Aug 2026: Q2 FY27 earnings call announces Nellore greenfield boards plant, Hyderabad expansion, and a cost‑out program at Parador; shares climb 24 % to ₹1,555.2.
  • Oct 2026 – Nov 2026: Q3 FY27 earnings call shows Parador still weak, India business solid; shares fall to ₹1,229.7.

What re‑rated it

  • Strong Pipes and Construction Chemicals volume and revenue growth in FY26.
  • Clean Coats acquisition adding high‑margin specialty chemicals.
  • New capacity at Nellore and Hyderabad boosting future earnings.
  • Cost‑out program at Parador expected to improve margins.

What de‑rated it

  • Persistent Parador losses and weak European demand.
  • Provision of ₹90 crore for Parador’s valuation hit.
  • Price pressure on PVC resin and other raw materials hurting margins.

News that moves this stock

  • Quarterly earnings calls and management commentary on India vs. Parador performance.
  • Announcements of acquisitions (Clean Coats, Crestia) and new capacity projects (Nellore, Hyderabad).
  • Parador cost‑out initiatives and European market outlook updates.
509675.sources: BusinessLine, The Hindu BusinessLine, BirlaNu investor relations, EarningsCalls.dev, BSE filings.

532522.one: Petronet LNG’s share price moved from Rs 313.85 to Rs 320.45, re‑rated on record profits, high volumes and new contracts, de‑rated on lower volumes, UoP dues and Gulf‑crisis‑related dips.
532522.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Price fell 27 % to 286.65 after Q3 FY25 results (Jan 27 2025) showed lower PBT/PAT and a 7 % drop in Dahej throughput.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: Price rose 12 % to 320.6 following Q4 FY25 results (May 19 2025) that delivered record PBT ₹5,275 Cr, PAT ₹3,926 Cr and the highest ever Dahej volume of 934 TBTU.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: Price fell 15 % to 271.9 after Q1 FY26 results (Jul 25 2025) revealed a 10 % rise in Dahej throughput but a 20 % drop in PBT/PAT.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: Price edged up 0.6 % to 273.6 following Q2 FY26 results (Nov 7 2025) that posted modest 4 % volume growth and PAT ₹806 Cr.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Price climbed 6 % to 290.4 after Q3 FY26 results (Feb 12 2026) with PBT ₹1,144 Cr, PAT ₹848 Cr and a 2 % volume increase.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: Price dropped 9 % to 263.6 after Q4 FY26 results (May 5 2026) that, despite record PBT ₹1,795 Cr and PAT ₹1,338 Cr, saw a 6 % volume decline due to a Gulf‑crisis‑driven dip in Dahej utilization.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: Price rose 7 % to 282.6 after Q1 FY27 results (Aug 19 2026) reporting the highest ever PBT/PAT for any first quarter.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Price surged 13 % to 320.45 following Q2 FY27 results (Nov 9 2026) that again delivered record PBT/PAT and strong operational efficiencies.

What re‑rated it

  • Record quarterly PBT/PAT and high Dahej throughput in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY27.
  • Highest ever capacity utilization at Dahej and Kochi terminals.
  • New long‑term LNG contracts with Exxon and Equinor, adding ~1 Mt/yr.
  • Diversification of supply sources (Oman, Mozambique, Nigeria, Congo, etc.) mitigating geopolitical risk.

What de‑rated it

  • Lower volumes and PBT/PAT in Q1 FY26 and Q4 FY26.
  • Gulf‑crisis‑related drop in Dahej utilization in March 2026.
  • Use‑or‑Pay (UoP) dues and new labour‑code costs impacting earnings.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcements of new long‑term LNG contracts or supply‑source diversification.
  • Updates on Dahej/Kochi terminal capacity expansion or utilization.
  • Geopolitical events affecting Qatar supply or Gulf‑region stability.
  • Regulatory changes (e.g., new labour codes) or UoP recovery announcements.
532522.sources: Business Standard, CNBC TV18, Petronet LNG press releases, InvestyWise, Inve Money.

500380.one: JK Lakshmi Cement was re‑rated from ₹697 to a peak of ₹991 as capacity‑expansion and an NCLT‑approved amalgamation lifted expectations, then de‑rated to ₹471 as seasonal demand weakness, cost‑inflation and a sharp Q2 FY27 profit slump eroded sentiment.
500380.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Expansion hype” – The company announced a double‑capacity grinding unit at Surat and a 2.3 Mt clinker line at Durg. The stock jumped 24 % to ₹864 (Nov 11 → Dec 9) before easing to ₹745 by Feb 2025 as the Q2 FY25 loss was digested.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: “Demand‑price squeeze” – Weak monsoon demand and five‑year‑low cement prices (Reuters Apr 2025) drove the share down 17 % to ₹672 (Jan 27 → Feb 24) and then a modest recovery to ₹861 (May 2025) on modest volume growth and a brief price‑recovery hint.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: “Amalgamation boost” – The NCLT’s sanction of the Udaipur‑Cement‑Works amalgamation (July 2025) and progress on the Durg expansion sparked a 21 % rally to a 2‑yr high of ₹991 (16 Jun → 14 Jul 2025).
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: “Profit‑slide correction” – Q4 FY25 PAT slipped 3 % YoY and cost‑inflation (fuel ₹1.82/kcal) resurfaced, pulling the price down to ₹821 (Aug 2025) and further to ₹759 (Oct 27 → Nov 24 2025).
  • Nov 2025 – Nov 2026: “Seasonal & cost headwinds” – Seasonal weakness, higher blended power cost and a 75 % YoY PAT fall in Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) forced a steep decline to ₹471 (Feb 23 → Mar 23 2026) and continued down‑trend to the current ₹470.55.

What re‑rated it

  • Announcement of major capacity additions (Surat grinding unit, Durg clinker line).
  • NCLT‑approved amalgamation scheme delivering expected synergies.
  • Rising non‑cement revenue (RMC ₹86 cr, AAC ≈ ₹70 cr) and premium‑product mix target of ≈ 30 %.
  • Management’s upbeat H2 FY27 demand‑price outlook in the Q2 FY27 call.

What de‑rated it

  • Sharp profit declines in Q2 FY25 (‑91 %), Q3 FY25 (‑52 %) and Q2 FY27 (‑75 %).
  • Persistent cost‑inflation (fuel ₹1.82/kcal, power ₹6.24/unit) and seasonal demand slowdown.

News that moves this stock

  • Updates on the Durg expansion timeline or completion of the Surat grinding unit.
  • Any large government or infrastructure orders (e.g., metro, housing) that boost cement demand.
  • Regulatory changes affecting cement pricing, GST or fuel subsidies.
500380.sources: Reuters, Business Standard, Quartr earnings summary, Livemint, Moneycontrol.

544213.one: From a high of ₹317 in early 2025 to a low of ₹110 in Nov 2026, Aelea Commodities was first re‑rated by a capacity‑expansion announcement and strong FY‑27 top‑line growth, then de‑rated as logistics‑driven working‑capital bloat and project delays ate earnings, leaving the stock flat‑lined at its 2‑year low.
544213.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Share fell from ₹220.65 to ₹210.1 as FY‑25 Q4 results showed modest revenue (≈₹182 cr) and only ₹1 cr PAT, with management flagging commodity‑price volatility and inventory build‑up.
  • Dec 2024 – Jan 2025: A 41 % jump to ₹317.15 followed the company’s public filing announcing completion of its Phase‑1 plant (140 MT/day) and a 60 MT capacity‑addition plan, signalling full‑capacity utilisation and a sizable order‑book.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: Price slid to ₹183.25 as Q1 FY‑25 earnings confirmed flat PAT despite higher volumes, and investors priced‑in the upcoming capital spend.
  • Aug 2025 – Sep 2025: A 24 % rise to ₹199.55 came after the board disclosed that 81 % of Q2 FY‑25 capacity was booked and that the new Surat land acquisition (₹114 cr) was approved, boosting growth expectations.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: The stock fell to ₹151.45 when Q4 FY‑25 results (₹182 cr revenue, ₹1 cr PAT) highlighted margin pressure from raw‑nut price spikes and higher working‑capital needs.
  • Oct 2026 – Nov 2026: A brief rally to ₹210.1 was driven by Q2 FY‑26 results (₹173.69 cr revenue, ₹8.70 cr PAT) showing a 56 % YoY revenue jump and a clearer path to full‑capacity utilisation.
  • Nov 2026 – Present: H1 FY‑27 earnings (₹24,674 cr revenue, ₹864 cr PAT) revealed 42 % top‑line growth but flat profit as logistics‑driven working‑capital and project delays offset gains; the board’s approval of a ₹114 cr Surat expansion (60 MT + 30 MT Cardanol) added a short‑term boost but also heightened debt, pushing the share down to ₹110.3.

What re‑rated it

  • Completion of Phase‑1 plant and announcement of a 60 MT capacity addition (Dec 2024).
  • Approval of the ₹114 cr Surat land acquisition and expansion plan (Aug 2025).
  • Strong FY‑27 H1 revenue growth (+42 % YoY) and 100 % capacity utilisation in H2 FY‑26 (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Persistent raw‑cashew price spikes and extended West‑Africa transit times inflating working‑capital (Nov 2026).
  • Project‑delay‑related cost overruns and logistics bottlenecks that kept PAT flat despite revenue gains (H1 FY‑27).

News that moves this stock

  • Capacity‑addition approvals (land acquisition, new processing units).
  • Logistics or geopolitical events affecting West‑African cashew imports (e.g., Strait of Hormuz disruptions).
  • Quarterly earnings that show PAT turning positive after the expansion completes (FY‑27 onward).
544213.sources: Moneycontrol, ScanX, StockSena, BSE filing, Arthneeti.

544609.html:
Physicswallah Ltd (PWL.NS) – One‑liner
Re‑rated from ₹134.31 to ₹126.65 after a series of earnings beats, AI‑driven growth, and a strategic M&A play that lifted the stock from a 2026‑03 low of ₹82.99 to a 2026‑07 high of ₹147.43.

How the story unfolded

Nov 2025 – Nov 2025 – Listing debut – Shares surged 49 % to ₹161.99 on the first day, closing at ₹134.31.
Feb 2026 – Mar 2026 – Tax demand shock – A ₹263 cr income‑tax notice on 16 Mar triggered a 29 % slide to ₹82.99.
Mar 2026 – Apr 2026 – Q4 FY26 results – May 27 earnings showed a 51 % revenue jump and EBITDA turning positive, lifting the price to ₹109.22.
Jun 2026 – Jul 2026 – New batch launch & AI push – The 29 Jun launch of PW Yakeen 2.0 2027 and AI‑powered “Infinity Pro” ecosystem spurred a 38 % rally to ₹147.43.
Aug 2026 – Nov 2026 – Q1 FY27 earnings & M&A – August 17 results narrowed loss to ₹77.5 cr and revenue up 24 %, pushing the share to ₹124.58; a November 9 M&A move (sold FinZ loan book for ₹96 cr, bought 11 % stake in Sarrthi IAS) capped the rally at ₹126.65.

What re‑rated it

  • Q4 FY26 earnings: 51 % revenue growth, EBITDA margin 3.1 %, AI‑driven cost discipline.
  • Launch of PW Yakeen 2.0 2027 and “Infinity Pro” ecosystem, expanding the hybrid learning model.
  • Strategic M&A: divestiture of FinZ loan book and stake in Sarrthi IAS, signalling portfolio optimisation.
  • Strong Q1 FY27 results: loss narrowed to ₹77.5 cr, revenue up 24 %, and a positive outlook for FY27.

What de‑rated it

  • March 2026 income‑tax demand of ₹263 cr, perceived as a cash‑flow hit.
  • NEET‑UG exam delay in 2026‑27, causing a temporary dip in online enrolments and revenue.

News that moves this stock

  • Earnings releases that show revenue growth, EBITDA improvement, or loss narrowing.
  • AI‑driven product launches or hybrid‑learning expansions.
  • Strategic M&A or divestiture announcements that reshape the business portfolio.
  • Regulatory or tax notices that could impact cash flow.
544609.sources: Reuters, Economic Times, Moneycontrol, CNBC TV18, Whalesbook.

540203.one: Re‑rated from ₹802 → ₹558 as integration synergies, a 20 % upper‑circuit Q4 FY26 rally and the Furlenco acquisition lifted the stock, then raw‑material inflation and margin pressure in Q2 FY27 de‑rated it.
540203.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Dec 2024: “Revenue‑growth rally” – Q2 FY25 showed 32 % YoY revenue rise and 19 % mattress‑volume jump, pushing the share from ~₹788 to a 20 % high of ₹947.
  • Jan 2025 – Feb 2025: “Profit‑pressure dip” – Q3 FY25 profit fell 39 % YoY to ₹18.8 cr; the stock slipped to ₹775.
  • Mar 2025 – Jun 2025: “Turn‑around & profit surge” – Q4 FY25 profit jumped 597 % to ₹91 cr and a 20 % upper‑circuit to ₹652; a week later (late‑May) the rally continued to ₹737 on the profit surprise.
  • Jul 2025 – Oct 2025: “Integration benefits” – Q1 FY26 core EBITDA rose 42 % YoY, margins hit 11.7 % and new showrooms opened, lifting the price to ₹673.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Mixed half‑year” – Q2 FY26 profit slipped to ₹9.66 cr; the share fell to ₹583 despite a 3‑month‑ahead Q3 FY26 profit jump (₹52 cr).
  • Apr 2026 – Jun 2026: “Q4 FY26 fireworks” – Q4 FY26 profit surged 78 % to ₹161 cr, EBITDA rose 90 %, and a 20 % dividend was announced, sending the stock up 22 % to ₹639 before a modest pull‑back to ₹605.
  • Jul 2026 – Aug 2026: “Strategic acquisition” – Market priced in the October‑1 2026 conversion of Furlenco (House of Kieraya) into a subsidiary, driving the share to a 22 % high of ₹700.
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: “Margin squeeze” – Q2 FY27 earnings call highlighted strong top‑line growth but “significant margin pressure due to raw‑material inflation and geopolitical disruptions,” pulling the stock down to ₹558.

What re‑rated it

  • 32 % YoY revenue growth and 19 % mattress‑volume surge (Q2 FY25).
  • 597 % PAT jump and 20 % upper‑circuit in Q4 FY26, plus a 20 % final dividend.
  • 42 % YoY core EBITDA rise, 11.7 % margin improvement and 234 new showrooms (Q1 FY26).
  • Conversion of Furlenco (House of Kieraya) into a subsidiary, expanding the product portfolio and retail footprint.

What de‑rated it

  • 39 % YoY PAT decline in Q3 FY25, triggering a price dip.
  • Q2 FY26 PAT falling to ₹9.66 cr despite revenue growth, pressuring the share.
  • Q2 FY27 “significant margin pressure” from raw‑material inflation and geopolitical disruptions, eroding the recent rally.

News that moves this stock

  • Integration‑synergy updates (Kurlon, new showrooms, e‑commerce volume).
  • Major M&A or subsidiary conversions (e.g., Furlenco/House of Kieraya).
  • Raw‑material price shocks or margin‑impact disclosures (inflation, supply‑chain disruptions).
540203.sources: Economic Times, CNBC TV18, EquityBulls, Upstox, ScoutQuest.

543669.html:
Keystone Realtors story in one line:
Re‑rated from Rs 724.75 to Rs 343.5 because record pre‑sales and a strong asset‑light redevelopment strategy lifted the stock, while revenue dips, profit slumps and an accounting‑standard shift repeatedly pulled it back.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Q2 FY25 results – net profit 66 cr, pre‑sales 700 cr; price fell 16 % to 521.45 cr as revenue dipped 13.8 % and the market questioned the revenue‑recognition method.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: Q3 FY25 results – profit 64.8 cr, revenue down 28 %; price slid slightly to 518.75 cr, reflecting continued concern over the revenue‑recognition lag.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: Q4 FY25 results – profit 64.8 cr, revenue down 28 %; price dipped to 534.75 cr, market still wary of the revenue‑recognition issue.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: Q1 FY26 results – record pre‑sales 1,068 cr, profit 14.5 cr; price jumped 25 % to 648.85 cr, driven by the pre‑sales surge and a robust launch pipeline.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Q2 FY26 results – profit 8.55 cr, revenue 499 cr, accounting shift to percentage‑of‑completion; price fell 17 % to 490.35 cr as the market penalised the accounting change and profit slump.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: Q3 FY26 results – profit 5 cr, revenue 266 cr; price fell 17 % to 406.1 cr, reflecting weak earnings despite strong pre‑sales.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: Q4 FY26 results – profit 64 cr, revenue 1,596 cr, pre‑sales 13.46 bn, credit‑rating upgrade; price fell 9 % to 371.45 cr, market over‑reacted to the revenue‑recognition shift and remained cautious.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 results – record pre‑sales, profit 65.55

543482.one: Eureka Forbes was re‑rated from ₹594 to ₹372 as a “growth‑driven consumer‑durables play” after a partnership with Dixon, strong FY 26‑27 earnings and rating upgrades, but was de‑rated by a massive GST show‑cause notice and commodity‑price pressure.
543482.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025 : Early‑FY 25 slowdown – Management warned of a post‑festive inventory build‑up and rising input‑cost pressure; the stock fell from ₹594.8 to ₹492.15.
  • Apr 2025 – May 2025 : Earnings‑driven rally – Q2 FY 26 results showed 15 % revenue growth, record PAT and margin expansion; investors pushed the price up 30 % (₹494.9 → ₹642.05).
  • Jul 2025 – Nov 2025 : Strategic partnership boost – The July 2025 announcement of a manufacturing tie‑up with Dixon Technologies to build robotic vacuums sparked a fresh rally, taking the price to a 2‑year high of ₹651.1 (Nov 24 2025).
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026 : Rating‑upgrade lift – CARE upgraded the long‑term bank‑facility and issuer ratings to AA Stable (Nov 19 2025); the stock rose to ₹587.45 before slipping to ₹518.25 as investors priced‑in upcoming price‑rise plans.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026 : Q3 FY 26 caution – The Feb 5 2026 earnings call highlighted a temporary e‑commerce slowdown, inventory normalization and a one‑off labor‑code charge; the share fell 16 % in four weeks (₹515.1 → ₹429.95).
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026 : GST‑SCN shock – A ₹273 cr GST show‑cause notice from Uttar Pradesh (Sep 28 2026) triggered a 17 %‑plus drop (₹423.75 → ₹352.5) and a continued slide to the current ₹372.1.
  • Sep 2026 – present : Crisil upgrade amid weakness – Crisil upgraded the corporate rating to AA Stable (Sep 8 2026), but the negative GST news outweighed the rating boost, leaving the stock on a downtrend.

What re‑rated it

  • July 2025 – Dixon Technologies partnership – gave the company a clear path to scale robotic‑vacuum production and diversify revenue.
  • May 2025 – Q2 FY 26 earnings beat – 15 % top‑line growth, record PAT and margin expansion signalled a new growth inflection point.
  • Nov 2025 – CARE rating upgrade to AA Stable – reinforced the strong balance‑sheet and low‑debt profile, widening the valuation multiple.
  • Sep 2026 – Crisil rating upgrade to AA Stable – confirmed medium‑term business risk reduction and solid liquidity.

What de‑rated it

  • Sep 2026 – Uttar Pradesh GST show‑cause notice (₹273 cr) – raised concerns over a large, unexpected tax liability and potential cash‑flow strain.
  • Feb 2026 – Q3 FY 26 earnings call – highlighted post‑festive inventory build‑up, e‑commerce slowdown and a one‑off labor‑code expense, prompting profit‑margin worries.

News that moves this stock

  • Any new large‑scale partnership or OEM tie‑up (e.g., additional robotics or appliance manufacturers).
  • Quarterly earnings that show double‑digit revenue growth with margin expansion (especially in water‑purifier and emerging categories).
  • Regulatory or tax developments (GST notices, state‑level assessments, or changes in indirect‑tax policy).
543482.sources: Business Standard, CNBC TV18, Business Standard (Dixon partnership), CARE rating intimation (Nov 2025), Crisil rating rationale (Sep 2026), BSE earnings‑call transcript (Feb 2026), Investing.com earnings‑call transcript (Nov 2026).

532234.one: Re‑rated from Rs 219.9 to Rs 329 (+50 %) after a roller‑coaster of profit‑driven rallies and a mid‑2025 downgrade, driven by record half‑yearly results, commodity‑price spikes and the near‑completion of the 5th‑stream alumina refinery.
532234.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Profit surge, price slides” – Q2 FY25 net profit jumps 415 % to ₹1,062 cr; despite the earnings beat, the share falls from ₹219.87 to ₹181.63 as investors weigh higher alumina costs and a broader market pull‑back.
  • Mar 2025 – Apr 2025: “Downgrade shock” – ICICI cuts the target to ₹190 and moves to Hold (May 27 2025); the stock plunges 24 % from ₹187.87 to a low of ₹143.22 on 7 Apr 2025, the deepest 4‑week dip.
  • May 2025 – Nov 2025: “Commodity rally & Q4 profit boost” – May 21 2025 Reuters reports Q4 profit more than doubles on higher aluminium and copper prices; combined with Pottangi bauxite‑mine start‑up news (Dec 2025) the share rallies to ₹262.57 by Nov 2025.
  • Aug 2025 – May 2026: “Capacity expansion fuels surge” – Q1 FY26 (Aug 7 2025) shows 77 % profit rise and record domestic alumina sales; the 5th‑stream refinery reaches 90 % physical completion; the stock climbs to a 2‑year high of ₹403.60 in May 2026.
  • Jun 2026 – Nov 2026: “Record half‑year, then correction” – H1 FY27 (Nov 9 2026) delivers best‑ever revenue, PBT, PAT and EBITDA; 5th‑stream trials target Jan 2027 start, pushing the price to ₹438.75 on 13 Apr 2026; a September 2026 escrow‑agreement for Utkal coal mines and profit‑taking pressure pull the share back to ₹329 by 9 Nov 2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Record half‑yearly revenue (₹11,143 cr) and profit (₹3,837 cr) in H1 FY27.
  • Sharp commodity‑price rally (aluminium +17 % YoY, copper +10 % YoY) boosting margins.
  • Near‑completion of the 5th‑stream alumina refinery and brownfield smelter expansion, promising higher alumina realization and capacity.
  • Strong domestic and export alumina sales (209 % export surge in Q1 FY26).

What de‑rated it

  • May 2025 ICICI downgrade to Hold on expectations of subdued alumina prices and limited volume growth.

News that moves this stock

  • Commencement of production at the 5th‑stream alumina refinery (early 2027).
  • Final regulatory clearance for the Pottangi bauxite mines and Utkal coal‑mine escrow/clearance updates.
  • Major shifts in global aluminium/copper prices or Indian government tariff changes.
532234.sources: CNBC TV18, Reuters, Business Standard, Kalkine India, Economic Times.

544387.one: Desco Infratech was re‑rated from ₹192 to ₹264 and back to ₹164 as FY25 earnings and order‑book expansion sparked a rally, margin‑compression concerns and profit‑taking caused a slump, and a CBG‑sector acquisition plus FY26 double‑digit growth re‑rated it again.
544387.html:
How the story unfolded

May 2025 – Sep 2025: FY25 earnings boom – FY25 PAT jumped 173 % and revenue topped ₹59 cr; order‑book swelled to ₹3,270 cr. Share price climbed from ₹192 to ₹250 (+30 %).
Oct 2025 – Dec 2025: Post‑boom correction – After the August 2025 high ₹264.5, investors trimmed positions; price fell to ₹188 (‑25 %).
Jan 2026 – Mar 2026: Margin‑drag slump – FY26 guidance hinted at margin compression; no major new orders surfaced. Share price slid to ₹153 (‑18 %).
Apr 2026 – Jun 2026: Renewables re‑rating – April 2026 acquisition in the compressed‑biogas (CBG) sector and June 2026 commissioning of a 5 TPD CBG plant lifted sentiment; FY26 results (revenue +100 %, PAT +80 %) confirmed growth. Price surged to ₹212 (+38 %).
Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: Stabilising after rally – Mixed order flow and profit‑taking after the FY26 peak brought the stock down to ₹164 (‑22 %). Q2 FY27 call (Nov 9 2026) was positive but the rally stalled.

What re‑rated it

  • FY25 results: PAT +173 % and order‑book ₹3,270 cr (May 2025).
  • July 2025 order‑book increase to ₹2,330 cr (new CGD, MDPE, power contracts).
  • April 2026 acquisition in the compressed‑biogas sector.
  • June 2026 commissioning of Phase‑1 (1 TPD) of a 5 TPD CBG plant in Uttar Pradesh.
  • FY26 results (Sept 2026): revenue +100 %, PAT +80 %, order‑book > ₹370 cr, diversification into renewable energy.

What de‑rated it

  • FY26 commentary on operating‑margin compression and higher receivables.
  • Profit‑taking after the August 2025 peak and after the FY26 rally.
  • Absence of dividend (FY26) signalling cash‑re‑investment rather than shareholder return.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of large city‑gas distribution contracts (e.g., with Adani Total Gas, MNGL).
  • New CBG or hydrogen‑natural‑gas blending project wins, capacity expansions, or regulatory clearances.
  • Changes to borrowing limits, credit‑rating upgrades or downgrades, and major acquisitions in renewable‑energy segments.
544387.sources: Business Standard, ScanX, IAM Renew, Desco Infratech SEBI filings, Investing.com.

543220.one: Re‑rated from Rs 1006 → Rs 915 as a 2024‑25 acquisition‑driven rally and 2025‑26 capacity‑expansion boom lifted the stock, then de‑rated by a CGHS‑driven oncology revenue hit and modest Q4 FY26 profit.
543220.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Acquisition & analyst upgrade” – Jaypee Hospital buy‑out (Nov 12) and Citi’s price‑target lift (Nov 8) sparked a 17 % jump to ~Rs 1180; price settled back to ~Rs 1004 by Feb 2025.
  • Mar 2025 – Jun 2025: “Capacity rollout” – Announcements of new beds in Nagpur, Lucknow and Delhi (Nov 7 2024) and approval of a 712‑bed Lucknow greenfield project (May 2025) drove a 30 % rally, peaking at Rs 1279 in Jun 2025.
  • Jul 2025 – Feb 2026: “Execution & earnings lift” – First‑quarter FY27 results (Aug 2026) showed 16 % YoY revenue growth and 15 % EBITDA growth; Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) delivered 20 % revenue growth and 10 % PAT rise, keeping the stock near its 2025 high of Rs 1220 before a gradual pull‑back to Rs 1050 by May 2026.
  • Mar 2026 – Oct 2026: “Oncology & pricing pressure” – CGHS drug‑price revision forced the drop of high‑value chemo drugs, cutting oncology’s share of inpatient revenue from 26 % to 21 % (Nov 3 2026). Combined with margin pressure, the stock fell 20 % to Rs 815 in Oct 2026.
  • Nov 2026 – present: “Modest Q4 profit, bearish tone” – Q4 FY26 net profit rose 13 % YoY to Rs 342 cr, but the market remained cautious; the share closed at Rs 915 on 9 Nov 2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Jaypee Hospital acquisition (500‑bed NCR asset).
  • Citi’s price‑target raise to Rs 1,250 and reiterated “Buy”.
  • Consistent ARPOB growth (8‑9 % older, double‑digit new hospitals).
  • Large‑scale greenfield projects (712‑bed Lucknow, 400‑bed Delhi, 550‑bed Gurugram).
  • FY27 Q1/Q2 earnings beating revenue and EBITDA expectations.

What de‑rated it

  • CGHS reimbursement caps forcing discontinuation of high‑value oncology drugs, slashing oncology revenue share.
  • Margin pressure in Q4 FY26 despite profit growth, leading to a modest 1 % price dip.

News that moves this stock

  • Any further inorganic deals or stake purchases in high‑capacity hospitals.
  • Regulatory updates on CGHS or other government pricing that affect oncology drug margins.
  • Commencement of construction or operational milestones for the Lucknow, Delhi or Gurugram greenfield hospitals.
543220.sources: CNBC TV18, Investing.com, ETHealthWorld, Livemint, Business Standard.

530999.one: Balaji Amines slid from ₹2,032 to ₹1,796 (‑12 %) as earnings fell and volumes slipped, then surged to ₹2,134 (+24 %) on strong Q4 FY26 profit, DME plant commissioning and FY27 profit‑doubling, before easing back on volume‑pressure concerns.
530999.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Q3‑FY25 slump” – Q3 FY25 (Feb 2025) showed PAT down 24 % YoY to ₹31 cr, revenue and volumes falling, margins compressing. Share price fell 24 % (₹1,709 → ₹1,293).
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: “Stabilisation & capacity hints” – Q4 FY25 (May 2025) still posted a 41 % profit drop, but the company announced new ACN and NBPT projects and a greenfield solar plant, keeping the stock near its low (₹1,403). Q1 FY26 (Aug 2025) delivered flat‑to‑slightly‑better results and highlighted DME, N‑Methyl‑Morpholine and ACN projects, nudging the price up to ₹1,549.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Demand‑pressure phase” – Q2 FY26 (Nov 2025) reported muted pharma/agro‑chemical demand, PAT ₹37 cr, and a comment on lower offtake; Q3 FY26 (Jan 2026) confirmed soft volumes and PAT ₹31 cr, pushing the share down to a 2‑year low of ₹1,079.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: “Q4‑FY26 rebound & FY27 kick‑off” – Q4 FY26 (May 2026) posted a 62 % PAT jump to ₹65 cr and revenue growth, sparking a 50 % 4‑week rally to ₹1,706. Q1 FY27 (Aug 2026) delivered a 111 % profit surge to ₹78 cr, commissioned India’s first commercial‑scale DME plant and confirmed major specialty‑chem expansion, driving the price to a high of ₹2,134.
  • Nov 2026: “Profit‑take & volume worry” – Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) showed profit ₹67 cr (+95 % YoY) but noted volume pressure and raw‑material price volatility; the stock slipped back to ₹1,797.

What re‑rated it

  • Q4 FY26 profit jump (+62 % YoY) and revenue growth.
  • Commissioning of the 100 ktpa Dimethyl Ether plant (first commercial‑scale in India).
  • FY27 profit more than doubling (₹78 cr) and strong EBITDA margin expansion (26 %).
  • Announcement of ₹750 cr specialty‑chem expansion with Mega‑Project status.

What de‑rated it

  • Q3 FY25 profit fall (‑24 %) and volume decline.
  • Q2 FY26 muted pharma/agro‑chemical demand and lower offtake.
  • Q3 FY26 soft demand, profit down to ₹31 cr and margin squeeze.
  • Q2 FY27 volume pressure despite profit surge, prompting profit‑taking.

News that moves this stock

  • Commissioning of new capacity (DME, N‑Methyl‑Morpholine, Acetonitrile) – any update on start‑up dates or commercial production.
  • Large specialty‑chemical orders or government incentives (e.g., Mega‑Project status, PSI subsidies).
  • Raw‑material price swings or regulatory changes affecting methyl‑amine and derivative margins.
530999.sources: CNBC TV18, Moneycontrol, Balaji Amines Investor Relations PDFs, Indian Chemical News, MarketScreener.

542484.one: Re‑rated then de‑rated, from Rs 555 to Rs 348, as FY25‑FY26 growth lifted the stock and muted demand, higher discounting and senior‑management exits pulled it down.
542484.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Demand‑driven slump – Earnings showed a muted consumer environment, higher discounting and flat wholesale; the stock fell from 555 to 398.45.
  • Mar 2025 – Aug 2025: Growth‑driven rally – FY25 year‑end results delivered 8.5% sales growth, 70% PAT jump, EBITDA margin expansion (+100 bps) and a Rs 1.60 dividend; aggressive square‑foot expansion and high‑visibility brand collaborations (Orry, Jaipur royal tie‑up) pushed the price up to 500 + Rs.
  • Sep 2025 – May 2026: Profit‑pressure correction – Q1‑Q2 FY26 showed 16% revenue growth but margin pressure from higher advertising spend and a 9.6% YoY PAT decline; the stock slipped to 433 Rs.
  • Jun 2026 – Aug 2026: Strategic pivot – Announcement of a new shirt‑manufacturing facility in MP (3 lakh units/month) and record Q2 FY27 headline (highest ever revenue and EBITDA) lifted the price to 447 Rs.
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: De‑rating & sell‑off – Senior‑management resignations, a trading‑window closure and lingering concerns over discounting triggered a 15%‑plus sell‑off, taking the stock down to 348 Rs.

What re‑rated it

  • FY25 year‑end results: 8.5% sales rise, 70% PAT surge, EBITDA margin +100 bps, dividend Rs 1.60.
  • Q1 FY26 (Jul 2025): 16% revenue growth, 20% EBITDA jump, >30% online B2C growth, 15% retail LTL.
  • High‑visibility brand collaborations (Orry, Jaipur royal tie‑up) and 81 k sq ft net store addition.
  • Nov 2026 announcement of a 3 lakh‑unit/month shirt plant in MP, promising import substitution and margin protection.

What de‑rated it

  • Early‑2025 earnings call flagged muted demand, higher discounting and flat wholesale, sparking a 23% slide.
  • Q2 FY26 (Sept 2026) showed PAT down 9.6% YoY, flat margin and higher discounting despite revenue growth.
  • Aug 2026 senior‑management resignations and trading‑window closure triggered a 15% sell‑off.

News that moves this stock

  • Launch of new manufacturing capacity or import‑substitution projects (e.g., shirt plant, denim capacity).
  • Major brand collaborations or large‑scale store‑footprint expansions (new marquee U.S. Polo stores, FOFO openings).
  • Management changes, regulatory filings, dividend or ESOP actions that affect share supply.
542484.sources: Business Standard, Arvind Fashions Investor Relations PDFs, Moneycontrol quarterly data, BSE filing notices.

522215.html:
Story in one sentence: Re‑rated from Rs 373 to Rs 421 as a record‑size order book > ₹1,000 cr, a €20 m tunnel‑panel win and a new heavy‑equipment plant lifted the stock, after earlier de‑ratings from margin compression and order‑book shrinkage.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Post‑Q3 FY25 disappointment – Q3 FY25 showed modest revenue (+5 %) and a 27 % fall in PAT, while the order book grew only to ₹68,324 lakhs; the share slid from 373.2 to 271.85.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: FY25 year‑end profit surge & strategic milestones – Q4 FY25 profit more than doubled (PAT ₹3,164 cr, +114 %) and the order book rose to ₹57,506 lakhs; inauguration of the Anand Centre of Excellence and Kinam’s first oil‑&‑gas order drove the price up to 422.2.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: FY26 growth spike then margin squeeze – Q2 FY26 delivered 37 % revenue growth, EBITDA ₹8,000 lakhs and a record consolidated order book crossing ₹1,000 cr, pushing the stock to a 2‑year high of 486.3. Q3 FY26 revealed a 63 % EBITDA drop and Omeras integration losses, shrinking the order book to ₹65,339 lakhs and sending the price down to 322.9.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: FY26 year‑end pressure & early turnaround signs – Q4 FY26 showed 31.7 % revenue growth but EBITDA margin fell to 11 % amid Omeras losses; the order book fell sharply to ₹681.6 cr, keeping the share near its low of 317.35, with a slight rebound to 327.7 on announced capex for glass‑fused tanks.
  • Nov 2026 onward: FY27 re‑rating on record orders & capacity expansion – Q2 FY27 highlighted a consolidated order book > ₹1,000 cr, a €20.56 m Fehmarnbelt tunnel‑panel order for Omeras, and a new heavy‑equipment plant near Anand; the stock rallied to 420.95.

What re‑rated it

  • Record‑size order book > ₹1,000 cr (FY27).
  • €20 m international tunnel‑panel contract (Omeras, Nov 2026).
  • 37 % H1 FY26 revenue jump and EBITDA recovery.
  • Inauguration of the Anand Centre of Excellence and Kinam oil‑&‑gas order (FY25).

What de‑rated it

  • Q3 FY26 margin compression and Omeras integration loss.
  • Order‑book contraction to ₹65,339 lakhs (Q3) and ₹681.6 cr (Q4 FY26).
  • Heat‑transfer segment revenue decline in Q4 FY26.

News that moves this stock

  • Large infrastructure or offshore contracts (e.g., tunnel‑panel orders).
  • Completion or expansion of the Anand heavy‑equipment plant.
  • Significant jumps in the consolidated order book (crossing ₹1,000 cr).
522215.sources: hleglascoat.com (PDF releases), finance.yahoo.com, marketscreener.com, livemint.com, indianchemicalnews.com.

512455.html:
Lloyds Metals re‑rated from Rs 924 to Rs 1,918, then dipped to Rs 1,807, as green‑mining, pellet and steel expansion drove gains, while monsoon and debt concerns pulled back.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Green‑mining focus and cost‑efficiency push; price surged 37 % (1050.8 → 1441.25).
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: Pellet plant commissioning and margin lift; price climbed 26 % (1021.1 → 1287.25).
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: 1.2‑million‑tonne steel plant pre‑commissioning; price rose 24 % (1175.5 → 1458.9).
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: Chemaf debt restructuring announced and gold‑mining approval for 1.5 Mtpa; price fell 20 % (1348.8 → 1073.6).
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Monsoon‑driven weakness; price dropped 20 % (1423.55 → 1136.5).
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: Chemaf restructuring progress and steel plant nearing commissioning; price jumped 33 % (1278.3 → 1695.6).
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: Record Q1 FY27 earnings, margin expansion to 39.2 %; price peaked at 1918.6.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Record H1 FY27, debt reduction, price settled at 1807.

What re‑rated it

  • Pellet plant commissioning and margin expansion.
  • Steel plant pre‑commissioning and downstream integration.
  • Chemaf debt restructuring expected to cut net debt by $500 m.
  • Gold‑mining approval for 1.5 Mtpa at Thriveni Swarnagiri.
  • Green‑mining initiatives and cost‑efficiency focus.

What de‑rated it

  • Monsoon‑driven production slowdown and price weakness.
  • Initial uncertainty around Chemaf debt restructuring.

News that moves this stock

  • Chemaf debt restructuring milestones and debt‑reduction progress.
  • Steel plant commissioning dates and capacity ramp‑up.
  • Gold‑mining approvals and execution at Thriveni Swarnagiri.
  • Green‑mining and cost‑efficiency announcements.

524091.html:
Carysil’s story in one line:
Re‑rated from Rs 772.7 to Rs 1,036.05 in November 2025, then de‑rated to Rs 956.95 in November 2026, driven by US‑election‑linked demand surges, capacity expansion, and later freight‑cost headwinds and raw‑material inflation.

How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Price fell from 772.7 to 583.35 (‑28 %) as Red Sea freight spikes, raw‑material cost rise, and US sales decline hurt margins.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: Price rose from 583.35 to 650.05 (+11 %) after management highlighted order momentum, US election optimism, and a new capacity‑expansion program.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: Price climbed from 650.05 to 826.9 (+27 %) with robust domestic demand, export growth, and new product launches.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: Price surged from 826.9 to 1,036.05 (+25 %) following highest‑ever Q2 revenue, strong order book, and continued US election‑driven momentum.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Price slipped from 1,036.05 to 975.8 (‑6 %) as macro headwinds and freight costs crept back up.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: Price fell from 975.8 to 918.45 (‑6 %) amid continued freight‑cost pressure and US market slowdown.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: Price surged from 918.45 to 1,179.8 (+28 %) after announcing a 250k quartz and 150k steel sink capacity addition and new built‑in appliance line.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Price dropped from 1,179.8 to 956.95 (‑18 %) as freight and raw‑material costs rose again and US demand cooled.

What re‑rated it

  • Highest‑ever Q2 revenue and robust domestic demand reported in Q2 FY27.
  • Strong order momentum linked to US election outcome.
  • Capacity‑expansion program across quartz, appliance, and faucet segments announced in Nov 2026 investor deck.
  • New product launches (built‑in appliances, wine chillers) boosting order pipeline.

What de‑rated it

  • Red Sea freight cost spikes and raw‑material price inflation.
  • US market slowdown and freight headwinds.
  • Regulatory delays (BIS certification backlog) temporarily tightening inventory and cash flow.

News that moves this stock

  • Large export order announcements, especially from the US and UK.
  • Capacity‑expansion milestones and new plant openings.
  • Regulatory approvals or delays (BIS certification, export clearances).
  • Macro‑economic indicators affecting freight and raw‑material costs.

500413.one: Thomas Cook India swung from a re‑rating at ₹197 to a de‑rating at ₹151 (Dec 2024‑Jan 2025) after a profit plunge, then re‑rated again to ₹169 (May 2025) on a record FY25 pre‑tax profit, fell to a low of ₹85 (Oct 2026) on Middle‑East disruptions, and now sits at ₹101 (Nov 2026) after the NCLT‑approved demerger of its resorts business and a steady Q2 FY27 earnings call.
500413.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Dec 2024: Q2 FY25 earnings beat – net profit up 40 % and revenue +9 % lifted the stock from ₹197 to a 2‑month high of ₹217 (Dec 2).
  • Dec 2024 – Jan 2025: Q3 FY25 profit collapse – net profit fell 40 % to ₹50 cr; chairperson redesignated as non‑executive. Share fell 24 % from ₹199 to ₹152 (23 Dec 2024 → 20 Jan 2025).
  • Apr 2025 – Jun 2025: Record FY25 pre‑tax profit – PBT ₹3,784 cr, travel EBIT +29 %; stock surged 33 % from ₹127 to ₹170 (5 May 2025 → 2 Jun 2025).
  • Jan 2026 – Mar 2026: Geopolitical & trade headwinds – Middle‑East airspace closures and global trade worries hit travel margins; share slid 22 % from ₹113 to ₹89 (9 Feb 2026 → 9 Mar 2026).
  • Mar 2026 – Jun 2026: Resort demerger announcement – plan to spin‑off Sterling Holiday Resorts; stock rallied 23 % from ₹91 to ₹112 (25 May 2026 → 22 Jun 2026).
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: NCLT approval & Q2 FY27 positive call – demerger motion cleared (7 Nov) and Q2 FY27 showed strong India‑portfolio recovery; share steadied at ₹101 (9 Nov 2026).

What re‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 earnings beat with 39 % profit jump.
  • FY25 record pre‑tax profit and double‑digit travel EBIT growth.
  • Announcement of the Sterling Holiday Resorts demerger (capital‑light growth story).
  • Q2 FY27 call highlighting recovery in India travel and 21 % FY‑on‑FY growth in financial services.

What de‑rated it

  • Q3 FY25 net‑profit plunge (‑40 %) and leadership redesignation.
  • Middle‑East airspace closures that crippled the Digital Imaging Solutions segment.
  • Global trade‑risk sell‑off in Jan 2026 that hit travel‑sector sentiment.
  • FY26 Q4 profit drop (‑54 %) driven by continued Middle‑East disruptions.

News that moves this stock

  • Final NCLT approval and subsequent listing of Sterling Holiday Resorts.
  • Any escalation or de‑escalation of geopolitical tensions affecting Middle‑East travel corridors.
  • Quarterly updates on financial‑services volume growth and forward‑booking pipelines in the India travel segment.
500413.sources: Business Standard, Moneycontrol, Reuters, TradeBrains, TTR Weekly, Thomas Cook India investor PDFs.

539787.one: From Rs ≈ 470 → ≈ 740 → ≈ 588, HCG was re‑rated on strong revenue‑mix upgrades, KKR’s takeover and aggressive capacity/tech expansion, then de‑rated by profit‑pressure, a trade‑margin cap and an EPCG provision.
539787.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Q2 FY25 beat – 14 % YoY revenue rise to ₹553 cr, PAT ₹18 cr and EBITDA margin ≈ 19 % lifted the stock 14 % (₹468 → ₹531).
  • Feb 2025 – Aug 2025: KKR takeover & capacity push – KKR bought a controlling stake (June 2025), rights issue cut debt, and Q3‑Q4 FY25 showed record revenue (₹559 cr) and margin recovery, driving the price to ₹661 (+19 % in 4 weeks).
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: FY26 momentum & institutional buying – Q1‑Q2 FY26 delivered 16.8 % revenue growth, Motilal Oswal funds lifted holdings above 5 % and a Kenya investment was announced; the stock peaked at ₹740 (+12 % in 4 weeks).
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Earnings dip & regulatory worries – Q2 FY26 profit before tax fell 28 % despite revenue up, and early chatter on a trade‑margin cap on anti‑cancer drugs sparked a 21 % slide to ₹582.
  • Feb 2026 – Aug 2026: Recovery & scale‑up – Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 showed 14‑19 % revenue growth, 146 new operational beds, MR‑LINAC, CAR‑T and robotic surgery launches; the share rose to ₹714 (+23 % in 4 weeks).
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 headwinds – Revenue up 15.8 % but PAT slipped 9 % and a Rs 116 m EPCG provision plus the newly effective trade‑margin cap (mid‑single‑digit EBITDA hit) pushed the price down to ₹588 (‑18 % in 4 weeks).

What re‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 earnings beat with higher ARPP and 18.8 % EBITDA margin.
  • KKR’s controlling‑stake acquisition, rights‑issue debt reduction and announced 1,000‑bed target.
  • Divestment of the non‑core Milann fertility business (June 2026) sharpening the oncology focus.
  • Deployment of high‑value tech (MR‑LINAC, CAR‑T, robotic surgery) and 54 % YoY international revenue jump.

What de‑rated it

  • Q2 FY26 profit‑before‑tax drop 28 % despite revenue growth.
  • Trade‑margin cap on non‑scheduled anti‑cancer drugs (effective Nov 2026) projected mid‑single‑digit EBITDA drag.
  • One‑off EPCG export‑obligation expense of Rs 116 m and lingering regulatory uncertainty.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcements of new bed capacity, brownfield openings or major acquisitions/divestments.
  • Government or regulatory changes to drug pricing (trade‑margin caps, price‑capping rules).
  • Large institutional stake moves or rights‑issue outcomes that affect capital structure.
539787.sources: Economic Times (ETHealthWorld), Moneycontrol, GuruFocus, NSE filing (press release 05 Nov 2026), Business Standard (KKR takeover), Moneycontrol (Motilal Oswal stake increase).

526299.html:
Mphasis stock re‑rated from Rs 2,839 to Rs 2,455, rising on AI‑led wins and acquisitions, falling on margin pressure and deal slowdown.

How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: MoneyGram‑Haas partnership and appointment of Mike Meyer boost confidence; price climbs to Rs 3,195.4 (+12 %) before easing to Rs 2,554.25.
Feb 2025 – Mar 2025: Q1 FY26 results reveal 3.5 % revenue growth but margin contraction; price drops 20 % to Rs 2,302.25.
Apr 2025 – Jun 2025: Q2 FY26 results show 17 % revenue lift, AI‑led deals hit 63 %; price surges 14 % to Rs 2,600.4 then 15 % to Rs 2,924.2.
Jan 2026 – Mar 2026: Q3 FY26 results highlight BFS slowdown and acquisition costs; price falls 17 % to Rs 2,296.5.
Apr 2026 – Aug 2026: Q4 FY26 results deliver best sequential growth in three years; price climbs 18 % to Rs 2,462.2, then Q1 FY27 results (July 2026) show strong AI wins and raised guidance; price dips to Rs 2,083.2 before rebounding to Rs 2,545 in Aug 2026.
Nov 2026: Investor deck announces continued AI momentum and Red Oak contract acquisition; price settles at Rs 2,455.

What re‑rated it

  • AI‑led deal wins rising from 12 % to 63 % of pipeline, driving revenue growth.
  • Strategic partnership with MoneyGram‑Haas and appointment of Mike Meyer signalling large‑deal focus.
  • Red Oak contract acquisition ($28 m) expanding service portfolio.
  • Consistent high‑single‑digit to low‑double‑digit revenue guidance and raised FY27 outlook.

What de‑rated it

  • Margin contraction due to ramp‑up costs and acquisition impact.
  • BFS segment slowdown amid macro uncertainty.
  • Temporary dip in deal pipeline during Q3 FY26.

News that moves this stock

  • Large AI‑led contract wins and outcome‑pricing deals.
  • Strategic acquisitions or contract novations (e.g., Red Oak).
  • Guidance revisions and earnings surprises.
526299.sources: Business Standard, Economic Times, Mphasis Investor Deck (Nov 2026)

532356.one: TRIVENI fell from Rs 499.6 to Rs 239.8 – a de‑rating – as strong Q2‑FY26 earnings and a record order‑book lifted the stock, but successive sugar‑cane yield shortfalls, harsh ethanol‑tender terms, water‑business execution lag and an El‑Niño‑driven monsoon scare drove brutal sell‑offs.
532356.html:
How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Dec 2024: “Order‑book hype” – Management highlighted an all‑time order‑book of ₹2,071 cr (Nov 5 2024) and a modest loss, yet investors focused on the booking surge, pushing the price from ₹377.5 to ₹399.1 and then to a 25 % high of ₹499.6 by 23 Dec 2024.

Jan 2025 – May 2025: “Profit‑turnaround optimism” – Q4‑FY25 results showed a 13.6 % PAT rise to ₹183 cr and 25 % revenue growth (May 28 2025). The beat on earnings and record engineering orders lifted the share to ₹430.1 by May 2025.

Jun 2025 – Aug 2025: “Margin pressure & execution lag” – August 2025 Q1‑FY26 report revealed 23 % revenue growth but an 80 % profit drop in sugar, higher maize costs and slower water‑business execution (Aug 5 2025). The market punished the stock, sliding to ₹331.8.

Sep 2025 – Nov 2025: “Ethanol‑capacity expansion” – November 2025 Q2‑FY26 disclosed a 15 % revenue rise, a swing to profit (₹21.4 cr) and a ₹1,000 cr ethanol‑capacity plan (Nov 6 2025). Positive guidance nudged the price up to ₹365.1.

Jan 2026 – May 2026: “Sugar‑realisation boost” – February 2026 Q3‑FY26 PAT surged 82 % (₹77.8 cr) on higher sugar realisations and lower maize costs (Feb 5 2026). The rally carried the stock to ₹385.2 by Feb 2026, then modestly back to ₹374.2 in May.

Jun 2026 – Jul 2026: “Rainfall risk & tender pain” – Q2‑FY27 commentary (Nov 10 2026) warned of unseasonal UP rainfall and tougher ethanol‑tender terms; combined with a sharp fall in sugar‑cane crush, the share plunged 52 % to ₹221.5 by 27 Jul 2026.

Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “Water‑business slowdown” – H1‑FY27 water‑revenue fell 13 % and PBIT dropped 56 % (Sept 2026 presentation), reinforcing the downtrend to ₹239.8 by 9 Nov 2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Record order‑book (₹2,071 cr) and engineering order surge (Nov 2024).
  • Q4‑FY25 profit beat and 25 % revenue jump (May 2025).
  • FY26 Q3 PAT surge +82 % on higher sugar realisations and lower maize costs (Feb 2026).
  • FY26 Q2 profit swing and ₹1,000 cr ethanol‑capacity expansion plan (Nov 2025).

What de‑rated it

  • Sharp sugar‑cane yield/crush decline and 80 % profit fall in sugar (Aug 2025).
  • Tough new ethanol‑tender terms and unseasonal UP rainfall risk (Jul 2026).
  • Water‑business EPC execution slowdown, revenue‑PBIT plunge (Sept 2026).

News that moves this stock

  • Updates on sugar‑cane crush, recovery rates and monsoon forecasts.
  • Government ethanol‑blending policy changes or new tender specifications.
  • Progress on the water‑business EPC pipeline and any major order‑book revisions.
532356.sources: Business Standard, Moneycontrol, ScanX, Whalesbook, The Hindu Business Line, Multibagg.ai, NSE/SEBI filings.

544286.company: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd
544286.html:
Niva Bupa’s story in one sentence:
Re‑rated from ₹74.02 to ₹90.41, then de‑rated back to ₹75.66, because early IPO enthusiasm, a record Q4 FY25 profit jump, followed by mixed quarterly results and a premium‑price hike in FY26, all of which the market rewarded or punished.

How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Dec 2024: IPO launch – Shares listed at ₹78.14, a 5.5 % premium to issue price; price surged to ₹83.6 (+13 %) as investors chased the new listing.

Jan 2025 – Apr 2025: Q4 FY25 results – 31 % net‑profit jump to ₹206 cr, GWP ₹2,395 cr, market share 9.4 %; price climbed to ₹90.41 (+19 %) as the market celebrated the strongest quarterly performance yet.

May 2025 – Aug 2025: Q1 FY26 results – GWP up 31.7 %, PAT ₹137.8 cr, combined ratio 100.2 %; price fell to ₹81.93 (≈‑10 %) as the market questioned the 100 % ratio and higher expense mix.

Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: Q2 FY26 results – Net loss ₹35.27 cr, GWP ₹2,108 cr, combined ratio 111.7 %; price slid to ₹76.57 (≈‑6 %) after the loss and high ratio, despite a 95.2 % claim‑settlement ratio.

Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Q3 FY26 results – 26 % growth, PAT ₹208 cr, combined ratio 102.9 %; price held near ₹76.24, reflecting a muted reaction to solid but not spectacular results.

Feb 2026 – May 2026: Q4 FY26 results – PAT up 80 %, GWP ₹8,586 cr, combined ratio 101.4 %; price rose to ₹79.83 (+4 %) as the market rewarded the strong year‑end performance.

May 2026 – Aug 2026: Q1 FY27 results – Retail growth outpaced the market, PAT ₹137.8 cr, combined ratio 100.2 %; price climbed to ₹82.72 (+4 %) on the back of improved profitability and market‑share gains.

Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 results – PAT doubled to ₹136 cr, GWP ₹2,484 cr, combined ratio 98.8 %; price fell to ₹75.66 (≈‑9 %) as the market corrected after a peak and weighed the higher premium hike announced for FY27.

What re‑rated it

  • Record Q4 FY25 profit surge and GWP growth.
