508814.one: Re‑rated from ~₹777 to ~₹826 as specialty‑film earnings beats, new high‑capacity lines and US market wins lifted the stock, while margin pressure from commodity BOPP, US tariffs and one‑off inventory losses pulled it back.
508814.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Early earnings boost then setback – Q2 FY24‑25 results (13 Nov 2024) showed specialty sales at 70% of volume and EBITDA growth, sparking a 28 % rally to ₹954. Later, the same release flagged a one‑time inventory loss and raw‑material price dip, and Q3 FY25 (11 Feb 2025) disclosed a line breakdown and BOPP margin pressure, driving the price down to ₹646.

  • Apr – May 2025: Capacity launch & Q4 beat – Announcement of the new 81 k t p.a. BOPP line and CPP line start (May 2025) plus a strong Q4 FY25 earnings beat (20 May 2025) sent the stock soaring 103 % to ₹1,188.

  • Aug – Nov 2025: New BOPP line ramps up, then margin drag – Q1 FY26 results (13 Aug 2025) highlighted a 19 % volume rise from the newly commissioned BOPP line and higher specialty margins, lifting the price to ₹1,017. Q2 FY26 (11 Nov 2025) warned of BOPP/BOPET margin compression, US tariff impact and stabilization costs, pulling the stock back to ₹790.

  • Jan – May 2026: US tariff worries and Q4 surge – Early‑year earnings showed modest growth, but the Q4 FY26 beat (20 May 2026) with 41 % volume growth, specialty‑film strength and near‑breakeven Plastech drove a 24 % rally to ₹815.

  • Aug – Nov 2026: FY27 momentum – Q1 FY27 concall (14 Aug 2026) confirmed all B2B units profitable and flexible‑packaging momentum, pushing the price to ₹938. Q2 FY27 concall (10 Nov 2026) delivered 51 % sales growth and 38 % EBITDA rise, stabilising the stock around ₹826.

What re‑rated it

  • Specialty‑film sales reaching >70 % of total volume.
  • Commissioning of high‑capacity BOPP, CPP and 16 k t coating line plus 10 k t 9‑layer barrier line.
  • Strong US market performance and new B2B contracts.
  • Consistent double‑digit EBITDA growth in FY27 Q1‑Q2.

What de‑rated it

  • One‑off inventory loss and raw‑material price shock (Q2 FY24‑25).
  • Line breakdown and BOPP margin pressure (Q3 FY25).
  • US tariff exposure and commodity‑film margin compression (Q2 FY26).

News that moves this stock

  • Announcements of new film‑line commissioning or capacity ramp‑up.
  • Large specialty‑film order wins, especially from US/EU customers.
  • Regulatory or tariff changes affecting BOPP/BOPET margins.
508814.sources: Cosmo First press releases (cosmofirst.com), Business Standard, Marketscreener, ICICI Direct, BSE India.

543626.one: EMIL swung from Rs 173 → Rs 130 → Rs 119 → Rs 133 → Rs 102 → Rs 120 → Rs 189 → Rs 143 as earnings turned from profit‑dragging FY26 quarters to record‑breaking FY27 results, powered by aggressive store roll‑outs and margin expansion, then trimmed on profit‑taking.
543626.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Festive‑season optimism fades” – CFO highlighted double‑digit festive growth (Nov 2024) and a strong wedding‑season outlook, but Q4 FY24 profit fell 22 % YoY (₹0.56 EPS). Stock slid from Rs 173.43 to Rs 130.36.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: “Quarterly profit rebound” – Q2 FY25 showed revenue +14.8 % YoY (₹1.59 Cr) and profit up 14.8 % YoY (₹0.42 EPS). Market rewarded the turnaround, pushing price to Rs 131.96.
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: “Modest growth, store‑opening noise” – Q3 FY25 revenue barely rose (+2.9 %) while profit slipped 6 % YoY; a new 9,500 sq ft store opened in Gurugram (30 Aug 2025) gave a tiny bump but price fell to Rs 119.22.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: “FY26‑FY27 launchpad” – Q4 FY26 (Jan‑Mar 2026) delivered a 39 % revenue jump and a 458 % profit surge (₹3.14 EPS), sparking a rally to Rs 132.69.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Seasonal soft‑spot, profit‑taking” – Despite Q1 FY27 record results (Apr‑Jun 2026), the market trimmed expectations ahead of the festive lull, dropping to Rs 102.32.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: “H1 FY27 momentum” – Q2 FY27 (Jul‑Sep 2026) posted revenue +19 % YoY and PAT +149 % YoY (₹40 Cr), widening EBITDA margin; price rebounded to Rs 119.89.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: “Expansion‑driven breakout” – Management announced Kolkata entry (15 stores by FY27) and a 25‑30‑store FY27 plan; aggressive cluster expansion and margin‑rich mature stores drove a 58 % 4‑week surge to Rs 189.44.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “Profit‑taking & guidance” – Q2 FY27 confirmed strong results but the market booked gains, pulling back to Rs 142.93.

What re‑rated it

  • FY27 Q1/Q2 earnings: revenue +39 % YoY, PAT +450 % YoY, EBITDA margin up 4 pp (Arthneeti, Oct 2026).
  • Aggressive store pipeline: 25‑30 new stores FY27, 15 in Kolkata, 30 in West Bengal (investor deck, Nov 2026).
  • Margin improvement in mature stores (11.2 % EBITDA) and faster same‑store sales growth (10‑12 % SSSG) (Arthneeti, Oct 2026).
  • Seasonal demand spikes: festive‑season double‑digit growth (Nov 2024) and strong summer demand (Q1 FY27).

What de‑rated it

  • FY26 Q1‑Q3 profit compression (PAT fell 22 % YoY, EPS down to ₹0.56) despite revenue growth, prompting the Feb 2025 dip.
  • Seasonal soft‑spot between summer and festive quarters (Q2 FY27) led to short‑term profit‑taking in Feb 2026.

News that moves this stock

  • Store‑network announcements – new multi‑brand openings, especially in West Bengal/Kolkata or other Tier‑2 metros.
  • Quarterly earnings with margin guidance – any surprise in EBITDA margin expansion or profit per share.
  • Capex & property acquisition updates – large land‑buy deals for store clusters (e.g., ₹50 Cr Kolkata property plan).
543626.sources: Marketscreener earnings releases, Moizz quarterly data, EquityBulls store‑opening note (30 Aug 2025), Arthneeti Q1 FY27 analysis (Oct 2026), NDTV Profit CFO interview (16 Nov 2024).

544600.one: Lenskart was re‑rated from Rs 409 to Rs 719 as the IPO filing, SEBI nod and blockbuster FY27 earnings lifted the stock, while a Q4‑FY26 profit dip briefly de‑rated it.
544600.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: IPO‑driven rally – filing for a Rs 2,150 cr IPO (Jul 29 2025) and SEBI approval (Oct 6 2025) pushed the share from Rs 409 to Rs 502 (+23%).
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: Profit‑pressure dip – Q4‑FY26 PAT fell 7.5 % to Rs 203.6 cr (revenue up 45 %) and component‑cost headwinds hit sentiment, pulling the price to Rs 469 (‑12%).
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: FY27‑Q1 re‑rating – Q1‑FY27 PAT surged 182 % to Rs 228 cr, revenue +34 % and product margin crossed 70 %; store‑densification and AI‑enabled smart glasses “B by Lenskart” were highlighted, lifting the stock to Rs 612 (+30%).
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: FY27‑Q2 momentum – Q2‑FY27 PAT more than doubled to Rs 232 cr, revenue +32.5 %; same‑store sales +20.8 % and international margins >10 % reinforced growth, taking the share to a 2‑year high of Rs 719 (+17%).

What re‑rated it

  • IPO filing and SEBI clearance (July 2025 & Oct 2025).
  • FY27‑Q1 earnings: PAT Rs 228 cr, revenue Rs 2,214 cr, product margin 70.3 %.
  • Aggressive store densification (≈ 540 net new stores FY26) and AI‑driven manufacturing.
  • FY27‑Q2 earnings: PAT Rs 232 cr, revenue Rs 2,845 cr, same‑store sales +20.8 %, international store count +22.

What de‑rated it

  • Q4‑FY26 profit dip to Rs 203.6 cr (‑7.5 %) amid higher component and inventory costs.

News that moves this stock

  • Final IPO pricing, listing date and fresh‑issue allocation.
  • Launch of next‑gen smart‑glasses or AI‑enabled eye‑care services.
  • Major international store roll‑out or acquisition of a regional eyewear brand.
544600.sources: Business Standard, Reuters, Economic Times, Hindu BusinessLine, Indian Express.

544014.one: Honasa Consumer was de‑rated from ₹371 to ₹222 in early 2025 after a Q2 FY24 loss, then re‑rated to a two‑year high of ₹503 by Aug 2026 as revenue‑led growth, new‑category launches and operating leverage accelerated.
544014.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Loss shock & sell‑off” – Q2 FY24 posted its first post‑IPO loss (‑₹41 cr) and a 30 % share‑price plunge (371 → 222 Rs). Analysts cut targets and downgraded the stock.
  • Apr 2025 – Nov 2025: “Turn‑around rally” – Q3 FY25 returned to profit (PAT ≈ ₹26 cr) and Q4 FY25 showed 7 % YoY revenue growth, sparking a 42 % four‑week jump (232 → 329 Rs) and a steady climb to ₹292 by Nov 2025. Distribution‑strengthening and a 22 % YoY revenue rise in Q2 FY26 (adjusted for Flipkart settlement) kept momentum.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: “Scaling the core” – Focus‑category revenue grew >35 % YoY; volume‑led growth of 30.5 % in Q1 FY27 and 31.8 % YoY revenue (₹756 cr) lifted the stock to ₹301 and then ₹354 Rs.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “Peak performance” – Q1 FY27 delivered record revenue (+32 %) and EBITDA >2× YoY (₹110 cr, 14.6 % margin). Q2 FY27 added 36 % revenue growth, PAT ₹73 cr (+87 %) and EBITDA near‑doubling, pushing the price to a two‑year high of ₹503 on 08‑Oct‑2026, before a modest pull‑back to ₹478 by 11‑Nov‑2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Consistent top‑line acceleration – 32 % YoY revenue growth in Q1 FY27; 36 % YoY in Q2 FY27.
  • Operating leverage – EBITDA margins rose from 7.7 % (FY26) to 14.6 % (Q1 FY27) and 12.7 % (Q2 FY27).
  • Brand‑level milestones – Two ₹1,000 cr ARR brands (Mamaearth, The Derma Co.) and successful entry into fragrance (FIKN) and hair‑colour categories.
  • Distribution overhaul – Shift to direct‑distribution in top‑100 cities, 40 %+ GT & MT growth, outlet reach >3 lakh stores.

What de‑rated it

  • Q2 FY24 loss – First quarterly loss since listing, prompting analyst downgrades and a 30 % price collapse.
  • Flipkart settlement change – Accounting impact in Q2 FY26 created a temporary revenue‑recognition dip, briefly unsettling investors.

News that moves this stock

  • New‑category launches (e.g., hair‑colour, fragrance, oral‑care) and associated revenue guidance.
  • Distribution‑channel updates – Progress on direct‑distribution rollout or major GT/MT partnership announcements.
  • Quarterly earnings beats – Surpassing revenue or EBITDA expectations, especially from core brands (Mamaearth, The Derma Co.).
544014.sources: Reuters, Moneycontrol, CNBC TV18, Honasa Investor Presentations (Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27, Q2 FY26, Q1 FY26), Business Standard (Q3 FY25 profit rebound).

544407.one: From Rs 256.99 in Jun 2025 to Rs 266.15 in Nov 2026, Aegis Vopak made a round‑trip re‑rating – IPO hype and FY25 earnings lifted it, debt‑financing worries pulled it down, then the Pipavav ammonia acquisition and record H1 FY27 performance drove a fresh re‑rating.

  • Sep 2025 – Dec 2025: FY25 earnings & capacity roll‑out – strong Q4 FY25 profit growth, commissioning of the Mangalore and JNPA liquid terminals, and a record‑high EBITDA lifted the price to ₹259.60.

  • Apr 2026 – Aug 2026: Pipavav ammonia terminal & Q1 FY27 momentum – announcement and completion of a ₹525 cr ammonia terminal at Pipavav, plus a positive Q1 FY27 call, sent the share to a 4‑week high of ₹284.50.
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: Global Tristar acquisition & Q2 FY27 results – the US$809 m Tristar acquisition was disclosed, creating regulatory‑approval uncertainty; despite a record H1 FY27 performance, the stock slipped to ₹266.15.

  • FY25 Q4 results: EBITDA +30 % YoY, PAT +34 % YoY, and full commissioning of new liquid terminals.

  • FY25 revenue fell 4 % YoY, prompting concerns over top‑line momentum.

  • Pending regulatory approvals and integration risk for the US$809 m Tristar acquisition created uncertainty.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of large strategic acquisitions (e.g., Tristar Holdings, global energy‑logistics assets).
  • Commissioning or acquisition of new storage capacity (LPG, ammonia, cryogenic terminals).
  • Regulatory clearances for major deals or pipeline projects (e.g., Kandla‑Gorakhpur LPG corridor).

543308.one: KIMS went from Rs 560 → Rs 727 (2024‑Nov → 2026‑Nov) as aggressive expansion and strong top‑line growth re‑rated the stock, but profit‑margin squeezes and debt‑burden spikes periodically de‑rated it.
543308.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Strong Q2 FY25 results” – Q2 FY25 profit rose 24% QoQ, new hospitals in Kerala and Nashik went live; the stock climbed from 560 to 581.
  • Feb 2025 – May 2025: “FY25 Q3‑Q4 earnings beat” – Q3 FY25 net profit jumped 81% YoY after the Chalasani Hospitals acquisition; Q4 FY25 profit surged 47% YoY with revenue up 25.7% and a new Thane unit opened. Share price surged to 640 then 745.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: “Ramp‑up pains” – Q1 FY26 showed 27% revenue growth but a 10% PAT dip as newly‑commissioned beds in Thane, Nashik and Kollam burned cash; Q2 FY26 profit plunged 38% YoY, margins halved and interest expense doubled. The stock fell back to 665.
  • Feb 2026 – May 2026: “Stabilisation & QIP deleveraging” – Q3 FY26 posted record‑breaking revenue > ₹1,000 cr, PAT ₹52 cr, and management signalled breakeven at new Bangalore/Thane sites; Q4 FY26 continued revenue momentum and the company completed a qualified institutional placement (QIP) to cut leverage. Share price recovered to 761.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “FY27 growth, profit‑taking” – Q1 FY27 (Aug 2026) highlighted strong revenue growth and successful deleveraging; Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) delivered growth across all metrics and a solid ramp‑up of new units, but the steep run‑up prompted profit‑taking and a pull‑back to 721 before a modest rebound to 727.

What re‑rated it

  • Robust top‑line expansion – FY25‑FY26 revenue CAGR ≈ 20% driven by new hospitals (Kerala, Thane, Bangalore) and strategic acquisitions (Chalasani, Sunshine).
  • Successful asset‑light O&M deals – 15‑year Operations & Management agreement for a 150‑bed Guntur super‑specialty hospital (June 2025) and similar contracts in Hyderabad & Maharashtra boosted future cash‑flow expectations.
  • Deleveraging via QIP – FY27 QIP raised fresh equity, cutting net‑debt‑to‑equity from 1.15× to a lower level, reassuring investors about balance‑sheet risk.
  • Strong occupancy gains in mature clusters – Telangana/Telangana beds operating at 75‑80% occupancy, delivering higher ARPOB and reinforcing cash‑flow visibility.

What de‑rated it

  • Margin compression during ramp‑up – Q2 FY26 PAT margin fell to 7.5% (‑800 bps YoY) as interest expense doubled and depreciation rose > 60%; new facilities burned cash.
  • Debt‑burden surge – Long‑term debt jumped ≈ 78% YoY to ₹1,654 cr in FY25, pushing interest coverage to a historic low of 4.5×, spooking investors.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of new hospital commissions or O&M agreements (especially in Tier‑2 cities or new metros).
  • Quarterly earnings showing margin recovery or debt‑reduction progress (e.g., QIP completions, breakeven at newly‑opened units).
  • Major acquisition or stake‑sale of a material subsidiary (e.g., Chalasani, Sunshine, or a large‑capacity Bangalore asset).
543308.sources: Moneycontrol, Business Line, AlphaStreet, MarketsMojo, AlphaStreet Q3 FY26 transcript.

530813.one: KRBL fell from Rs 275.85 to Rs 268.2 in early 2025 on profit weakness and legal worries, then rallied to Rs 415.45 by Nov 2026 as booming domestic demand, record revenue and a cash‑rich balance sheet re‑rated the stock, while export‑related headwinds periodically knocked it down.
530813.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Profit dip & legal cloud – Sep 2024 results showed a 33 % profit fall and ongoing ED attachment on land assets; the share slipped to Rs 268.2 (its 2025 low).
  • Mar 2025 – May 2025: Domestic rebound – March 2025 results posted a 9.4 % YoY sales rise, driven by higher branded‑pack volumes; the stock jumped to Rs 323.95.
  • Jul 2025 – Aug 2025: Record domestic revenue – Q2 FY26 (Sept 2025) delivered the highest ever quarterly revenue, with domestic sales up >30 % YoY; the rally peaked at Rs 473.3 on 18 Aug 2025.
  • Sep 2025 – Nov 2025: Export shock – Export volumes to the Middle East fell sharply amid logistics disruptions and a partial Strait‑of‑Hormuz closure; the share fell to Rs 429.35.
  • Feb 2026 – Mar 2026: West‑Asia conflict fallout – Export revenue dropped 31 % YoY in Q2 FY27, and geopolitical tension hit sentiment; the price slid to Rs 287.35.
  • Mar 2026 – Apr 2026: Mixed Q1 FY27 but strong profitability – Q1 FY27 call highlighted record profitability, cash strength and domestic growth despite export headwinds; the stock rebounded to Rs 359.9.
  • Jul 2026 – Aug 2026: Record Q2 FY27 revenue – Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) posted the highest ever quarterly revenue, domestic sales up 33 % YoY, offset by a 31 % export decline; the rally lifted the price to Rs 437.65.
  • Nov 2026 – present: Consolidation – Continued domestic momentum, accelerating consumer‑pack volumes and a solid balance sheet kept the stock climbing to Rs 415.45.

What re‑rated it

  • Domestic revenue surged +30 % YoY in Q2 FY27, the strongest ever quarterly top line.
  • Branded‑pack and regional‑rice volumes grew ≈ 25 % YoY, expanding market penetration.
  • Cash & bank balances topped Rs 1.8 trillion, giving flexibility for inventory build‑up and brand investment.
  • Market‑share leadership (≈ 85 % of global basmati trade) reinforced pricing power and brand premium.

What de‑rated it

  • Export volumes to the Middle East fell ≈ 11 % YoY in Q1 FY27 and overall export revenue dropped 31 % YoY in Q2 FY27 due to logistics disruptions and the Strait‑of‑Hormuz issue.
  • Ongoing Enforcement Directorate attachment on land assets created legal uncertainty and pressured sentiment.

News that moves this stock

  • Resolution of the ED/land‑attachment case – clearance would remove a major regulatory drag.
  • New long‑term distribution partner in Saudi Arabia or other West‑Asia markets – would revive export volumes and margins.
  • Significant domestic pack‑volume orders or price‑realisation upgrades – would boost revenue and sustain the re‑rating momentum.
530813.sources: Moneycontrol, Yahoo Finance (earnings‑call transcripts), BSE investor presentation (Q2 FY27), KRBL corporate filings.

544008.one: From Rs 496.7 in Nov 2024 to Rs 534.75 in Nov 2026, MAXESTATES was re‑rated by capital‑raise and blockbuster pre‑sales news, then de‑rated by a GST tax notice, delivering a net round‑trip gain of ~+7 % with two sharp rally phases.

How the story unfolded

  • Mar 2025 – Apr 2025: “Stabilisation” – No major news; price held near Rs 410‑420.
  • May 2025 – Jun 2025: “Pre‑sales acceleration” – FY26 integrated report (Jul 2026) highlighted 5‑fold YoY pre‑sales growth to ₹5,305 cr and 100 % commercial occupancy, lifting the stock 34 % (385.6 → 517.7).
  • Mar 2026 – Apr 2026: “RERA approval boost” – Mar 7 2026 RERA clearance for Max One revived the stalled Delhi‑One project; price jumped 19 % (330.65 → 393).
  • Jul 2026 – Aug 2026: “Q1 FY27 pre‑sales explosion” – Aug 21 2026 Q1 call disclosed 5× YoY pre‑sales (≈₹1,100 cr) and 100 % commercial occupancy; stock surged 37 % (393.2 → 539.05).
  • Sep 2026 – Oct 2026: “GST tax notice shock” – Jul 28 2026 GST show‑cause notice on subsidiary Pharmax (₹5.9 cr demand) dented sentiment; price fell 21 % (594.65 → 471).
  • Nov 2026: “Q2 FY27 sustenance pre‑sales” – Nov 11 2026 Q2 call reported sustained pre‑sales of ₹2,100 cr and healthy cash collections; stock rallied to Rs 534.75.

What re‑rated it

  • Rs 800 cr QIP & Rs 150 cr warrant issue (Sep 2024) – fresh equity capital signalled growth funding.
  • Massive pre‑sales growth (Q1 FY27, Aug 2026; FY26 report, Jul 2026) – 5× YoY residential bookings and ₹5,305 cr FY26 pre‑sales.
  • 100 % occupancy of commercial assets – stable annuity income (₹120‑125 cr FY25, >₹158 cr FY26).
  • RERA approval for Max One (Mar 2026) – cleared a long‑stalled project, restoring buyer confidence.

What de‑rated it

  • GST show‑cause notice on subsidiary (Jul 2026) – ₹5.9 cr tax demand raised regulatory risk concerns.

News that moves this stock

  • New large‑scale land acquisitions or joint‑development MoUs (e.g., Indirapuram & West Delhi MoUs, Aug 2026).
  • Further pre‑sales milestones or launch of flagship residential projects (Estate 361, Max One).
  • Regulatory clearances or setbacks (RERA, GST, tax notices) affecting project timelines.
544008.sources: Max Estates website, CNBC‑TV18, Economic Times (ETRealty), Business Standard, TipRanks, ScanX Trade.

543954.one: From Rs 37.6 (Nov 2024) to Rs 26.9 (Nov 2026), Allcargo Terminals has been a re‑rated‑then‑de‑rated round‑trip, driven first by FY 25 earnings disappointment, then by capacity‑expansion and volume‑growth news that lifted the stock, before a fresh slowdown pulled it back, and finally by a Q2 FY 27 profit surge that restored some upside.
543954.html:

Global trade slowdown concerns and a weaker outlook pushed the price down to Rs 27.8 by Feb 2025.

  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: “January volume surprise” – A January 2025 update reported 11 % YoY CFS volume growth, sending the share up ~9 % (intraday high Rs 29.3). The price recovered to Rs 28.0 by August.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: “Capacity rollout & strong Q2 FY 26” – Announcement of the 25‑acre JNPT expansion and the renewed 5‑year Mundra contract, plus Q2 FY 26 showing 12 % YoY volume growth, lifted the stock to a 2‑year high of Rs 31.5.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Trade‑headwinds hit again” – Slowing container traffic and a muted FY 26 outlook dragged the price down to Rs 25.3.
  • Feb 2026 – Aug 2026: “Capex‑build‑phase, Q1 FY 27 steady” – Farukhnagar Private Freight Terminal construction stayed on track; Q1 FY 27 call highlighted 7 % YoY volume growth but profit pressure from one‑off tax on JV dividends. The stock fell to a 2‑year low of Rs 23.7.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “Q2 FY 27 profit surge & capacity news” – Q2 FY 27 delivered a 228 % PAT jump, 12.6 % YoY volume growth, and confirmation that Farukhnagar PFT will be ready by Mar 2027 plus a 60 k‑TEU JNPT expansion. The stock rebounded to Rs 26.9.

What re‑rated it

  • Capacity expansion announcements – JNPT 25‑acre yard, Mundra lease renewal, Farukhnagar PFT (on‑track for Mar 2027) and Speedy JNPT 60 k‑TEU addition.
  • Strong volume growth – 11 % YoY CFS volumes in Jan 2025; 12.6 % YoY in Q2 FY 27.
  • Margin improvement – Operating margin rose to 23.4 % in Q2 FY 27; EBITDA per TEU above ₹2,000 for eight straight quarters.
  • Digital & efficiency upgrades – MyCFS platform adoption (≈70 % of customers) and rollout of a Smart Yard Management System.

What de‑rated it

  • FY 25 earnings miss – Q4 FY 25 net loss from accelerated amortisation and tax impacts.
  • Macro‑trade slowdown – IMF/World Trade outlook revisions and weaker global container traffic cited in FY 25‑26 calls.
  • Contract‑renewal uncertainty – Lingering questions on the Mundra lease extension and potential land‑acquisition costs.

News that moves this stock

  • Capacity‑completion updates – commissioning dates for Farukhnagar PFT, JNPT expansion, and any new ICD roll‑outs.
  • Quarterly volume & margin guidance – especially any deviation from the 12 % YoY volume growth target or margin guidance.
  • Regulatory / contract outcomes – renewal of the Mundra lease, land‑acquisition approvals, or major partnership deals (e.g., Speedy Multimodes stake).
543954.sources: Business Standard, Avsar AI, Investor Stack, Allcargo Terminals investor presentations, Economic Times (ET Infra).

524332.html:
BCL Industries story in one sentence:
BCL Industries de‑rated from Rs 52.78 to Rs 29.9, because earnings volatility, a fire‑related shutdown, rising maize costs and regulatory shifts in the ethanol tender outweighed capacity expansion and new ENA contracts.

How the story unfolded

Dec 2024 – Jan 2025:
- ENA letter of acceptance announced; stock peaked at Rs 56.56 on 2 Dec.
- Price slumped to Rs 37.38 by 18 Feb as market priced in margin pressure from the edible‑oil exit.

Feb 2025 – May 2025:
- Q4 FY25 earnings and dividend declaration lifted shares to Rs 39.97 by 30 May.

May 2025 – Aug 2025:
- Minor rally to Rs 41.02 by 1 Aug, then fell to Rs 37.95 by 30 Nov after weaker ENA volumes.

Nov 2025 – Mar 2026:
- Fire at Sangat Kalan ethanol plant in June 2026 caused a 2‑month shutdown; price dropped to Rs 29.74 by 18 Feb and hit a 2‑yr low of Rs 26.79 on 23 Mar.

Apr 2026 – Oct 2026:
- New 150 KLPD distillery commissioned; CBG plant plan announced; shares recovered to Rs 33.51 by 31 May and Rs 35.63 by 18 Aug.
- Regulatory tightening on ethanol tender and rising maize prices pushed price back to Rs 29.62 by 11 Nov.

Nov 2026:
- Q2 FY27 earnings call highlighted margin pressure from maize price hikes and tender changes; shares settled at Rs 29.9 on 11 Nov.

What re‑rated it

  • ENA order from Rajasthan State Ganganagar Sugar Mills (Nov 2024).
  • Q4 FY25 results and dividend announcement (May 2025).
  • Expansion of grain‑based ethanol capacity to 1,150 KLPD (Nov 2026).
  • Strategic pivot to IMFL and CBG (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Fire‑related shutdown of 200 KLPD ethanol plant (June‑Aug 2026).
  • Rising maize prices and regulatory changes in the ethanol tender (2026).

News that moves this stock

  • New ENA or ethanol tender contracts.
  • Regulatory announcements on ethanol blending mandates or maize sourcing.
  • Operational disruptions (fires, shutdowns) or capacity expansion milestones.
524332.sources: Business Standard, Livemint, ScanX, BSE Investor Deck, BCL Industries earnings calls.

544454.one: From Rs 217.7 to Rs 189.2 – a round‑trip re‑rating driven by a high‑profile IPO, record FY‑26 earnings and FY‑27 revenue peaks, punctuated by loss‑narrowing scares, debt worries and FII outflows that forced sharp sell‑offs.
544454.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Jul 2025 – Oct 2025: IPO hype and early earnings – filing of an Rs 800 cr IPO (Nov 2024) and debut listing lifted the stock to Rs 217.7; modest slide to Rs 213.3 as investors priced in FY‑25 growth targets.
  • Oct 2025 – Jan 2026: Profit growth but lingering loss concerns – Q2 FY26 profit rose to Rs 28 cr, revenue up 38 % to Rs 354 cr and expansion into Indore, Kolkata and Mohali; market still penalised the stock, dropping to Rs 176 as debt‑servicing pressure and a loss‑making profile remained front‑stage.
  • Jan 2026 – Apr 2026: Loss‑narrowing but still negative – Q3 FY26 loss narrowed to Rs 17.07 cr (operating margin 60.9 %) yet interest expense surged and FII holdings fell sharply, pushing the price to a 52‑week low of Rs 133.55.
  • Apr 2026 – Jul 2026: Record FY26 results – Q4 FY26 delivered record revenue Rs 1,469 cr (+37 % YoY) and PAT Rs 125 cr (+145 %); launch of 4 MW solar plant and green‑power roadmap sparked a rally to Rs 179‑202, re‑rating the stock on profitability and sustainability.
  • Jul 2026 – Nov 2026: FY27 momentum and profit‑driven rally – Q1 FY27 posted highest‑ever quarterly revenue Rs 428 cr and strong operating leverage; Q2 FY27 showed robust YoY growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT, lifting the price to Rs 189.18 despite a brief pull‑back in Oct‑Nov on profit‑taking and CAPEX concerns.

What re‑rated it

  • IPO filing and listing (fresh capital, market visibility).
  • FY26 Q4 record revenue & profit plus 100 % green‑power rollout.
  • FY27 Q1/Q2 earnings with highest quarterly revenue and expanding EBITDA/PAT.
  • Large enterprise wins (1.4 L sq ft lease, 68 k sq ft design‑build) and entry into three new cities.
  • Operating margin above 60 % and rising value‑added services contribution (15‑18 %).

What de‑rated it

  • Persistent net losses and high interest burden (Q3 FY26 loss, debt‑to‑EBITDA > 7×).
  • Massive FII outflow (22.88 % to 2.30 % Jul‑Dec 2025) and occupancy dip to ~81 %.
  • CAPEX escalation and uncertainty around lease‑liability guidance.

News that moves this stock

  • Quarterly results showing >30 % YoY revenue growth and PAT turning positive.
  • Announcement of large enterprise leases or design‑build contracts (>1 L sq ft).
  • Updates on solar/green‑energy capacity or debt‑refinancing that improve interest coverage.
544454.sources: Moneycontrol, Economic Times, Markets Mojo, IndiQube investor presentations.

543932.one: Re‑rated from Rs 578 (Nov 2024) to Rs 714 (Nov 2026) as a wave of large defence orders, a Rs 500 cr QIP and a five‑fold revenue jump turned losses into profit and revived the order‑book.
543932.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Mar 2025: “Revenue slump & loss streak” – ESOP allotment announced (Nov 11 2024) but the company reported a sharp 80 % YoY revenue fall and a third consecutive loss in Q4 FY25 (May 8 2025). Share price fell from Rs 578 to a low of Rs 386.
  • Apr 2025 – Nov 2025: “Order win sparks bounce, then earnings disappointment drags” – After the Q4 loss, the stock rallied to Rs 560 (May 2025) on optimism, then slipped to Rs 447 (Aug 2025). A fresh defence win worth >₹100 cr (₹75 cr Army Zolt + ₹30 cr SWITCH 2) on Nov 14 2025 lifted the price to Rs 514 and closed the month at Rs 466.
  • Dec 2025 – Mar 2026: “Continued losses and low point” – Q1 FY26 posted a ₹23.5 cr loss and revenue down 85 % YoY (July 22 2025). The share slid to its 2‑year trough of Rs 333 on Mar 10 2026.
  • Apr 2026 – May 2026: “Capital infusion & revenue explosion re‑rates” – A Rs 500 cr Qualified Institutional Placement at ₹795 per share (June 2026) and a Q1 FY27 revenue jump to ₹68.6 cr (+436 % YoY) drove the price up 86 % to Rs 818 (May 4 2026) and peaked at Rs 945 on Jun 1 2026.
  • Jun 2026 – Nov 2026: “Profitability and order‑book execution fuels rally” – Management highlighted >20 % execution of the opening order book, record H1 revenue and a return to PAT in Q2 FY27 (Nov 2 2026). The stock rose to Rs 714 (Nov 11 2026).

What re‑rated it

  • Defence contracts totalling >₹100 cr (Nov 2025).
  • Rs 500 cr QIP that boosted cash and visibility (June 2026).
  • Q1 FY27 revenue surge >5× YoY and narrowing loss (Aug 2026).
  • Turn‑around to profit in Q2 FY27 and positive EBITDA (Nov 2026).
  • Strong order‑book execution (>20 % of opening book) and favourable defence procurement policy.

What de‑rated it

  • Government procurement slowdown causing an 80 % YoY revenue drop and consecutive loss quarters (FY25‑FY26).
  • Q4 FY25 loss and weak Q1 FY26 results that pushed the price to its 2‑year low.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of new MoD/Army drone contracts (especially >₹50 cr).
  • Capital‑raising events (QIP, preferential allotments) or major equity dilution.
  • Partnerships/JVs that secure NATO Stock Numbers or open US/foreign markets.
543932.sources: Moneyworks4me, Inc42, Livemint, Business Standard, Entrackr, Economic Times.

531548.one: Somany Ceramics was sharply de‑rated from ₹644 to ₹402 (Nov 2024 → Feb 2026) on profit‑dip and demand‑softness, then re‑rated to ₹549 (Nov 2026) as operational efficiencies, capacity‑utilisation gains, JV expansions and a 25 % revenue jump lifted earnings and margins.
531548.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Profit‑dip shock” – Q2 FY25 net profit fell 41 % YoY to ₹16.95 cr, EBITDA down 22 % (ConstructionWorld, 4 Nov 2024). Share price slid from ₹644 to ₹463.
  • May 2025 – Nov 2025: “Capacity‑ramp‑and‑mix pressure” – Q1 FY26 revenue rose 4.4 % but PAT fell ≈ 40 % YoY; management highlighted a new Max plant ramp‑up and cost‑control focus (AlphaStreet, 14 Aug 2025). Stock recovered to ₹511 by Aug 2025, then drifted to ₹441 by Nov 2025 as demand remained soft.
  • May 2026 – Apr 2026: “Margin‑turnaround” – Q4 FY26 profit jumped 77 % YoY to ₹37.8 cr, EBITDA margin rose 300 bps to 10.6 % and a ₹2 dividend was announced (CNBC TV18, 15 May 2026). Price rallied to ₹470 by Apr 2026.
  • May 2026 – Aug 2026: “FY27‑Q1 breakout” – Q1 FY27 profit surged > 240 % YoY, revenue up 24 % and EBITDA margin expanded to 11.5 % (NDTVProfit, 12 Aug 2026). Share price jumped to ₹523 by Aug 2026.
  • Nov 2026 – present: “Growth‑phase acceleration” – Investor deck (11 Nov 2026) showed FY27‑Q2 revenue up 25 % YoY, EBITDA margin improvement and a profitable JV turnaround; the company announced a new 9 + MSM tile plant in Tirupati and lifted its sanitary‑ware JV stake to 76 % (company releases, 4 Nov 2026). Stock climbed to a 2‑year high of ₹702 (Dec 2024) and settled at ₹549 on 11 Nov 2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Q4 FY26 profit surge & dividend – 77 % PAT jump and higher margin (May 2026).
  • Q1 FY27 earnings breakout – > 240 % PAT rise, 24 % revenue growth, EBITDA margin up 360 bps (Aug 2026).
  • FY27‑Q2 growth & JV upgrades – 25 % revenue growth, tighter control of the higher‑margin sanitary‑ware JV, and a new 9 + MSM tile plant expanding geographic footprint (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 profit dip – 41 % YoY PAT decline, cost pressure and demand slowdown (Nov 2024).
  • Q1 FY26 weak profit – ~ 40 % YoY PAT fall despite modest revenue rise, signalling margin pressure (Aug 2025).

News that moves this stock

  • Quarterly results showing double‑digit revenue growth and margin expansion (especially FY27 quarters).
  • Announcements of new capacity (tile plants, JV expansions) or increased stake in high‑margin sanitary‑ware businesses.
  • Dividend declarations or share‑buy‑back plans that signal cash generation.
531548.sources: Business Line, Construction World, CNBC TV18, AlphaStreet, NDTVProfit.

544315.one: Re‑rated from ₹827 to ₹227 as a post‑IPO hype surge was crushed by quarterly profit‑taking, governance concerns and a Gulf‑conflict supply‑chain shock, then briefly recovered on strong order‑book growth before sliding again on execution delays.
544315.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Dec 2024 – Mar 2025: IPO hype & profit‑taking – Listing at ₹827 (peak) followed by a sharp fall to ₹495 as investors booked gains after the IPO and digested FY 25 Q4 results that, while profitable, highlighted project‑lumpy revenue and governance questions.
  • Mar 2025 – Sep 2025: Order‑book optimism & governance drag – Share price rose to ₹587 on news of a growing order book (₹7,164 mn, +34% YoY) and new Mexico‑plant order, but slipped to ₹509 when proxy‑advisor criticism over board attendance and ESOP amendments surfaced (Sept 2025).
  • Sep 2025 – Mar 2026: Earnings pressure & supply‑chain shock – Q4 FY 25 showed modest revenue growth (3.4% YoY) and winding‑up of a subsidiary, pushing the stock down to ₹450 and then to a low of ₹263 as the Gulf conflict disrupted membrane shipments and Q1 FY 27 earnings warned of “near‑term supply‑chain disruptions”.
  • Mar 2026 – Jun 2026: Recovery on execution rebound – Q2 FY 27 call highlighted restored execution, a 34% order‑book rise and a new ₹14.25 cr solar‑PV order, lifting the price to ₹355.
  • Jun 2026 – Nov 2026: Volatility persists – Continued project‑lumpiness, slower O&M conversion and lingering logistics issues dragged the stock to ₹264 and then to the current ₹227 level.

What re‑rated it

  • IPO listing and strong FY 25 Q4 profit (+68% PAT) → initial surge.
  • FY 25 order‑book expansion (+34% YoY) and new Mexico/alcohol‑bev order → mid‑2025 rally.
  • Q2 FY 27 “execution improved” call, 34% order‑book growth and solar‑PV win → June 2026 bounce.

What de‑rated it

  • Post‑IPO profit‑taking and concerns over project‑lumpy revenue pattern.
  • Sep 2025 proxy‑advisor criticism on board attendance and ESOP amendment.
  • FY 25 Q4 modest revenue (+3.4%) and winding‑up of a subsidiary, plus forex loss on peso orders.
  • Q1 FY 27 supply‑chain disruption from the Middle‑East conflict, causing a loss and a 36% four‑week slide.

News that moves this stock

  • Large international project wins (e.g., Mexico plant, solar‑PV contracts) that boost the order book.
  • Resolution of Gulf logistics issues or any improvement in membrane supply from the UAE.
  • Governance updates (proxy‑advisor recommendations, ESOP implementation) that affect shareholder confidence.
544315.sources: Concord Enviro Systems FY 25 earnings PDF, AlphaStreet Q2 FY 27 transcript, AlphaStreet Q4 FY 25 transcript, Concord Enviro proxy‑advisor clarification (Sept 2025).

540762.one: Tube Investments fell from Rs 3,680 → Rs 2,286 (‑38 %) as profit‑pressure news de‑rated it, then rallied to Rs 2,754 (+21 %) on volume‑led e‑mobility growth and CDMO commissioning, before slipping again on steel‑price‑driven margin compression.
540762.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Profit‑pressure dip” – Q2 FY24 profit fell 14 % and expenses rose 18 %; the market punished the stock, driving it from Rs 3,440 to Rs 2,580 (‑24 %).
  • Apr 2025 – May 2025: “Fair‑value & dividend boost” – Q4 FY25 results showed a Rs 569 cr fair‑value gain on TI Clean Mobility CCPS and a Rs 2 dividend; strong mobility revenue lifted the share to Rs 3,045 (+22 %).
  • Oct 2025 – Feb 2026: “Flat‑to‑fall phase” – After a period of stability around Rs 3,060, rising steel prices and raw‑material cost pass‑through eroded margins, pulling the price down to Rs 2,499 (‑15 %).
  • Mar 2026 – May 2026: “Volume‑led recovery” – Q1 FY27 earnings call highlighted 17 % volume growth across engineering and e‑mobility, sending the stock up to Rs 2,850 (+18 %).
  • Sep 2026 – Oct 2026: “Margin‑compression slide” – Q2 FY27 mixed results flagged steel‑price spikes and high cell/BOM costs; the share fell 17 % to a two‑year low of Rs 2,080.
  • Nov 2026 – present: “Awaiting CDMO scale‑up” – Commissioning of a semi‑commercial CDMO plant and EV‑truck breakeven targets keep the stock hovering at Rs 2,276, with upside only on successful commercialisation.

What re‑rated it

  • Acquisition of 67 % of Kcaltech (aluminium‑tube business) – new addressable market.
  • Q4 FY25 fair‑value gain on Clean Mobility stake and a Rs 2 dividend.
  • Record‑high e‑mobility turnover in Q1 FY27, driven by strong volume growth.
  • Commissioning of the CDMO semi‑commercial plant and validation‑batch deliveries.

What de‑rated it

  • Q2 FY24 profit decline and higher expenses (Nov 2024).
  • Steel‑price inflation and high cell/BOM costs compressing margins (Q2 FY27).

News that moves this stock

  • Large EV‑truck or three‑wheeler order wins and volume updates.
  • Regulatory clearances or commercial‑scale shipments from the CDMO pharma plant.
  • Significant steel‑price or raw‑material cost changes affecting margin outlook.
540762.sources: Business Standard (Nov 2024 acquisition & profit‑decline), Business Standard (Aug 2026 Q1 FY27 rally), Quartr (Nov 2026 Q2 FY27 earnings summary), Business Standard (Nov 2026 Q2 profit growth), TI India press release (May 2025 Q4 FY25 results).

543463.one: From Rs 1,434 (Nov‑2024) to Rs 492 (Nov‑2026) – the stock was briefly re‑rated on a strong Q1‑FY27 profit surge and wedding‑season optimism, then de‑rated by a festive‑calendar shift, negative same‑store sales, and a legal‑metrology notice.
543463.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Jan 2025: “Q2 FY25 boom → peak” – Q2 FY25 showed 23 % revenue and 37 % PAT growth (Motilal Oswal target ₹1,500). Share price climbed to a 2‑yr high of ₹1,434 (25 Nov 2024) before slipping to ₹1,194 by 13 Jan 2025.
  • Jan 2025 – May 2025: “Q3 FY25 moderation” – Q3 FY25 (Dec 2024) delivered 7.8 % revenue growth but SSSG fell 4.2 % YoY. The stock drifted down to ₹751 by 1 May 2025.
  • May 2025 – Nov 2025: “FY26 slowdown” – No major earnings surprise; the market priced in weaker wedding‑season demand and a legal‑metrology show‑cause notice (₹50 k fee) that raised compliance concerns. Share price fell to ₹626 on 30 Nov 2025.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Deepening de‑rating” – Continued soft retail sales and a widening gap between revenue and PAT pushed the stock to a trough of ₹455 on 9 Feb 2026.
  • Feb 2026 – Aug 2026: “Q1 FY27 rally” – Q1 FY27 (Aug 2026) posted +7.2 % revenue, +14.7 % PAT and 3.8 % same‑store growth; management’s confidence in the upcoming wedding season sparked a bounce to ₹529 on 31 Aug 2026.
  • Aug 2026 – Nov 2026: “Q2 FY27 caution” – Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) saw only +2.4 % revenue growth, domestic SSSG –5.8 % and a festive‑calendar shift that delayed Navratri sales. The stock slipped back to ₹492 by 13 Nov 2026.

What re‑rated it

  • Q2 FY25 outperformance (23 % revenue, 37 % PAT) and a ₹1,500 target from Motilal Oswal.
  • Q1 FY27 profit jump (+14.7 % YoY) and 3.8 % same‑store sales growth.
  • Strong wedding‑season outlook and new brand campaigns (Manyavar “Made for Each Other”, Twamev “Truly You”).
  • Store‑network optimisation (net rollout of high‑performing EBOs).

What de‑rated it

  • Festive‑calendar shift (Navratri moved to Q3 FY27) curbing Q2 FY27 revenue (+2.4 % YoY) and causing –5.8 % same‑store sales.
  • Negative same‑store sales in Q3 FY25 (‑4.2 % YoY) and Q2 FY27 (‑5.8 %).
  • Legal‑metrology notice (₹50 k compounding fee) that signalled regulatory risk.

News that moves this stock

  • Wedding‑season demand data (booking trends, bridal‑wear orders).
  • Festive‑calendar announcements (timing of Navratri, Diwali, Shradh).
  • Regulatory/compliance updates (legal‑metrology, labeling or franchisee‑law notices).
543463.sources: Moneycontrol, Textile Insights, Vedant Fashions investor presentations (Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27, Q3 FY25), Motilal Oswal research.

544179.one: Go Digit fell from Rs 330.7 to Rs 252.6 – a 23 % de‑rating – as a soft market, falling motor rates and flood losses hurt earnings, while occasional profit jumps and a strong solvency ratio gave brief re‑ratings.
544179.html:
How the story unfolded

Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: Soft‑market shock – Premium‑rate cuts and rising claim costs forced a 10 % slide (330.65 → 296.85).
May 2025 – Aug 2025: Profit‑jump rally – Q1 FY26 showed PAT ↑ 59 % (₹ 161 cr) and GWP ↑ 12 %; the stock surged to a 2‑yr high of 355.35.
Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: Growth‑slowdown – GDPI fell 1‑2 % YoY, combined ratio drifted above 108 %; price slipped to 322.6.
May 2026 – Aug 2026: Underwriting strain – Q4 FY26 loss ratios rose to 73 % and motor OD premiums fell 40 %; share fell sharply to 259.65.
Nov 2026 – present: Cautious‑mixed phase – Q1 FY27 (Jul 2026) emphasized profitability over volume; Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) saw flood losses in Gujarat but a modest revenue rise; price now 252.6.

What re‑rated it

  • Q1 FY26 profit surge (PAT ₹ 161 cr, loss‑ratio 70.3 %) – drove a 21 % 4‑week rally (May 5 → Jun 2 2025).
  • FY25 full‑year profit more than doubled (PAT ₹ 425 cr, solvency 2.24×) – pushed the stock to its 2‑yr high (Aug 2025).
  • Strong solvency ratio (2.40× in Q2 FY27) and AUM growth + 15 % – gave a 20 % bounce after flood‑loss shock (Sept 14 → Oct 12 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Soft market & rate cuts (private‑car OD rates down 40 % in Apr‑May 2026) – triggered a 19 % 4‑week fall (Jun 29 → Jul 27 2026).
  • Gujarat & Northeast flood losses (₹ 63 cr in Q2 FY27) – eroded PAT and pulled the stock down to a 2‑yr low of 239.
  • Rising combined ratio (99.8 % in Q2 FY27, up from 94.9 % a year earlier) – kept investors wary despite revenue growth.

News that moves this stock

  • Regulatory rate‑change announcements (IRDAI motor‑TP or OD pricing reforms).
  • Large natural‑catastrophe loss updates (flood, cyclone or earthquake claims).
  • Reinsurance treaty terms or commission changes (especially any reduction in RI commission).
544179.sources: Business Standard, Kalkine India, Go Digit investor presentations, IRDAI releases.

544167.one: JNK India slid from Rs 658.5 to Rs 366.5 as the market first re‑rated the firm on booming H1‑FY25 revenue and marquee orders, then de‑rated it on profit‑margin erosion and legal friction, before a partial re‑rating in FY27 on a strong order book, a Nigeria export win and a renewable‑energy JV.
544167.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Dec 2024: “Revenue‑rocket & index boost” – FY25 H1 revenue jumped 47% YoY to ₹1,981 mn, order book swelled to ₹13,116 mn and the stock was added to the S&P Global BMI Index; price surged to a 2‑yr high of ₹658.5.
  • Jan 2025 – Apr 2025: “Profit‑pain & arbitration” – Q3 FY25 showed a 91% YoY PAT drop to ₹28.4 mn and a Reuters‑reported arbitration petition by Suntech (7 Feb); price tumbled 46% to ₹311.85.
  • May 2025 – Oct 2025: “Earnings‑drag” – Q4 FY25 revenue fell short of the prior year and net profit slipped to ₹132 mn; no fresh marquee wins surfaced, pushing the stock down to ₹283.75.
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “Bottom‑out & execution strain” – order‑book contraction and temporary Q2 execution hurdles drove the price to a 2‑yr low of ₹241.38.
  • Mar 2026 – May 2026: “Order‑book rebuild” – management highlighted a refreshed order pipeline and reaffirmed FY27 guidance, lifting the share 60% to ₹329.95.
  • Jun 2026 – Aug 2026: “FY27 Q1 beat” – Q1 FY27 call (19 Aug) delivered strong YoY revenue (+30%) and profit growth; price surged 53% to ₹456.25.
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: “Execution hiccup, export win & JV” – Q2 FY27 flagged temporary shipment delays, but the same period announced a Rs 500 cr Nigeria heater order and a 51:49 JV with Chemdist Technology; price fell 21% to ₹366.55.

What re‑rated it

  • 47% H1‑FY25 revenue surge and a ₹13,116 mn order book (Nov 2024).
  • Inclusion in the S&P Global BMI Index (Oct 2024).
  • Strong Q1 FY27 results: 30% YoY revenue growth, profit expansion and a ₹1,662 mn order book (Aug 2026).
  • Rs 500 cr export order from Nigeria and the Chemdist Technology JV (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Suntech arbitration petition (Feb 2025).
  • Q3‑FY25 profit collapse (PAT down 92% YoY) and Q4‑FY25 revenue decline (May 2025).
  • Execution delays and shipment‑hurdles in Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026).

News that moves this stock

  • Announcement of a ≥ Rs 300 cr export or large‑scale international order.
  • Launch or progress of the Chemdist Technology joint venture (renewable‑energy/low‑opex hydrogen).
  • Legal or arbitration developments affecting the company’s contracts.

544466.one: Re‑rated from Rs 1,090 to Rs 4,148 as a strategic L&T Semiconductor partnership, massive capacity upgrades, a Rs 1,500 cr QIP, and a 30 % stake in AI‑video‑compression firm BLUE drove explosive FY27 growth, while only modest profit‑taking after Q3 FY26 dented the rally.
544466.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Oct 2025 – Jan 2026: “Semiconductor partnership kick‑off” – The three‑year L&T Semiconductor tie‑up to make nine million IP cameras lifted the stock 36 % (₹1,057 → ₹1,435) and to ₹1,534 by Nov 2025.
  • Feb – Apr 2026: “Strong Q3 FY26 results, profit‑taking” – FY26 Q3 showed 37 % revenue growth and 99 % EBITDA jump, but the share slipped to ₹1,489 as investors trimmed positions after the earnings surge.
  • May – Aug 2026: “Capacity & product rollout surge” – Announcement of a new lens‑assembly line and Kadapa Phase III scale‑up sparked a 32 % rise to ₹2,508, then a 48 % jump to ₹3,709 after the Q1 FY27 call (89.5 % YoY revenue growth, margin expansion).
  • Sep – Nov 2026: “Funding, AI acquisition & debt‑free balance sheet” – QIP launch (Rs 1,500 cr) and a 30 % stake in BLUE (₹45 cr) were disclosed on 5 Nov, followed by the Q2 FY27 call (89.9 % YoY revenue growth, debt‑free status). The stock peaked at ₹4,213 on 2 Nov, then settled at ₹4,148 on 13 Nov.

What re‑rated it

  • L&T Semiconductor three‑year SoC partnership (Oct 2025).
  • Kadapa Phase III & Greater Noida capacity‑doubling plan (May 2026).
  • Q1 FY27 earnings: +89.5 % YoY revenue, margin expansion, robust cash flow (Aug 2026).
  • Rs 1,500 cr QIP funding and debt‑free balance sheet (Nov 2026).
  • 30 % stake in BLUE AI video‑compression firm, adding next‑gen tech to the portfolio (Nov 2026).

What de‑rated it

  • Profit‑taking after the strong Q3 FY26 earnings release (Feb 2026).

News that moves this stock

  • Award of large government or defence surveillance contracts.
  • Completion and commercial launch of Kadapa Phase III / Greater Noida plants.
  • Further AI‑video‑compression or semiconductor acquisitions that deepen the technology stack.
544466.sources: Aditya Group (adityagroup.com), Moneycontrol, Economic Times (ET), Livemint, CNBC TV18.

507552.one: From Rs 122.48 (Dec 2024) to Rs 45.61 (Nov 2026) the stock was de‑rated – a 63 % slide – as export‑logistics bottlenecks, weak Q2‑FY25 earnings and a war‑driven sales collapse crushed sentiment, while occasional capacity‑expansion announcements and a brief frozen‑food rally gave only short‑lived lifts.
507552.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Q2 FY25 disappointment” – Management warned of slow customer call‑offs, export‑shipping delays and a dip in tomato‑pulp volumes. The stock fell from 114.56 to 93.99 (‑18 %).
  • May 2025 – Aug 2025: “Q3 FY25 profit crash” – September 2025 results showed net sales up 14 % but profit collapsed 94 % (₹0.73 cr vs ₹7.14 cr a year earlier). The share slid from 95.3 to 78.45 (‑18 %).
  • Nov 2025 – Feb 2026: “FY26 Q4 sales slump” – FY26 Q4 (Mar 2026) disclosed a 32 % YoY sales drop to ₹248 cr, war‑related inventory issues and a modest profit rebound. The price tumbled from 78.45 to 60.93 (‑22 %).
  • Mar 2026 – Apr 2026: “Frozen‑food & capacity optimism” – Management highlighted a 28 % YoY rise in frozen‑food volumes and announced a new pulp line slated for commercial production in Jan 2027. The stock rallied to 57.21 (‑4 %).
  • Sep 2026 – Nov 2026: “Q2 FY27 mixed loss” – Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) reported a loss driven by adverse forex and renewed export‑logistics headwinds, despite strong volume growth. The share fell to a 2‑year low of 45.61 (‑20 %).

What re‑rated it

  • Capacity expansion announcements – New pulp line (commercial Jan 2027) and spray‑drying capacity boost (120 ktpa) signalled future volume upside.
  • Frozen‑food volume surge – 28 % YoY growth in FY26 lifted margins and attracted short‑term buying.
  • PLI incentive receipt – FY25 PLI claim of ₹33.86 cr booked in Q4 FY25 improved cash‑flow expectations.

What de‑rated it

  • Export‑logistics bottlenecks – Repeated vessel shortages and freight‑rate spikes cut export call‑offs, hurting top‑line.
  • Profit collapses – Q2 FY25 (‑94 % profit) and Q3 FY25 (net profit ₹0.73 cr) triggered sharp sell‑offs.
  • War‑related inventory & pricing pressure – March 2026 war impact forced inventory sales at 25 % lower realizations, eroding earnings.

News that moves this stock

  • Announcements of new processing capacity (pulp, spray‑dry, Tetra Recart) and commercial start‑up dates.
  • Export‑logistics updates – vessel availability, freight‑rate changes, or resolution of shipping delays.
  • Regulatory or subsidy changes – PLI claim approvals, export‑policy shifts, or tariff adjustments affecting mango/tomato pulp.
507552.sources: Moneycontrol, Foods & Inns investor PDFs (Q2 FY25 transcript, FY26 Q4 results, FY27 Q1 & Q2 call notes), Resultsiq (FY27 Q2 earnings summary).

531179.one: Arman Financial Services was re‑rated from Rs 1,275 to Rs 1,563 as AUM surged +50% YoY and record Q2‑FY27 profits validated a turnaround, while periodic regulatory‑guardrail scares and disbursement slow‑downs caused sharp pull‑backs.
531179.html:
How the story unfolded

  • Nov 2024 – Feb 2025: “Cautious‑growth” – Q2‑FY25 earnings call highlighted tighter underwriting and lower disbursements; despite the caution, the market nudged the share up to Rs 1,330 as investors priced in a modest earnings‑quality improvement.
  • Feb 2025 – Aug 2025: “AUM‑driven rally & first pull‑back” – H1‑FY25 showed AUM at Rs 2,465 cr and a 13% rise in PPoP, lifting the price to Rs 1,500. By Aug the stock slipped to Rs 1,372 as RBI‑guardrail chatter and a slowdown in fresh micro‑finance disbursements dented sentiment.
  • Aug 2025 – Nov 2025: “Recovery‑phase surge” – Management’s Q2‑FY26 call (Nov 2025) reported falling GNPA, higher collection efficiency and a 26% jump in disbursements, sparking a 26% rally to Rs 1,730.
  • Nov 2025 – May 2026: “Stabilisation & diversification” – H1‑FY26 results showed AUM growth of 29% YoY, strong MSME/LAP momentum and continued asset‑quality improvement, pushing the price to Rs 1,787.
  • May 2026 – Nov 2026: “Record‑profit climax & profit‑taking” – Q2‑FY27 (Nov 2026) delivered record quarterly PAT (Rs 97 cr) and AUM up 50.6% YoY, driving the price to a two‑year high of Rs 1,969. Subsequent profit‑taking and lingering regulatory uncertainty pulled the stock back to Rs 1,562.

What re‑rated it

  • Record Q2‑FY27 profit and PAT surge.
  • AUM expansion +50% YoY to Rs 3,209 cr (H1‑FY27).
  • Structural reforms (separate credit‑officer model, BCM rollout) cutting GNPA to sub‑4% across segments.
  • Diversification into higher‑margin MSME, two‑wheeler and secured LAP books, with LAP ticket size rising to ₹5‑7 lac.
  • CGFMU insurance covering ≈ 67% of the micro‑finance portfolio, lowering provisioning pressure.

What de‑rated it

  • RBI‑issued guardrails on interest rates and NIM caps, prompting a slowdown in fresh micro‑finance disbursements.
  • Periodic spikes in high‑yield micro‑finance pricing (≈ 34% yield) raising regulatory‑risk concerns.
  • Short‑term profit‑taking after the Q2‑FY27 beat.

News that moves this stock

  • RBI policy updates on interest‑rate caps, NIM limits or micro‑finance guardrails.
  • Quarterly AUM and PAT beats, especially when AUM growth exceeds +40% YoY.
  • Launch or scaling of the secured LAP segment and any new CGFMU/CGTMSE insurance approvals.
